focus: cards-first (Mastercard card-present and card-not-present) with UPI, account-to-account, wallet and token coverage for breadth

status_definitions.IMPLEMENTED: A dedicated transaction-level injector reproduces this attack's authorization footprint, and it is part of the default simulated mix.
status_definitions.PARAMETERIZED: Reachable today as a configuration of an existing injector through the attack-specification dials (amount, velocity, device, geography, merchant, timing) without new code, but not part of the default mix.
status_definitions.RESEARCH_ONLY: Catalogued and characterized — objective, GenAI role, kill chain, transaction and behavioural signature, authorization-time observability — but NOT simulated. Listed so the research surface is visible and not overstated.
status_definitions.FUTURE: Named as planned simulator work. Not simulated today.

honesty_note: This catalog deliberately describes far more attacks than the simulator implements. Every entry carries its simulator status, so breadth of research is never presented as breadth of simulation. Entries describe defender-observable consequences and signals only — no operational guidance, tooling, or bypass technique appears anywhere in this file.

attacks.name: Hyper-Personalized Cardholder Spear Phishing With Live OTP Relay
attacks.subcategory: Targeted phishing / credential and AFA harvesting
attacks.attacker_objective: Obtain full card credentials plus the live additional-factor (OTP/3DS) response from a specific cardholder so a card-not-present purchase or card tokenization can be completed in real time.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Language models turn thin public and leaked context — employer, city, recent merchant relationships, language preference — into individually tailored lures that read like genuine issuer or merchant correspondence, with none of the grammar and formatting tells that legacy phishing filters and user training relied on. The same models generate matching landing-page copy and support-chat replies, so the pretext stays consistent when the victim asks questions. The effect for defenders is that per-victim content uniqueness rises sharply, collapsing the value of content-hash and template-similarity detection.
kill_chain: target enrichment from breached and public data
credential and AFA capture on lookalike page
real-time relay to a live CNP authorization
attacks.transaction_signature: The payment-stream footprint is weak: authorization arrives as an ordinary 3DS-attempted or successful CNP purchase with genuine PAN, correct CVV and a correct OTP, so most issuer rules see a well-authenticated transaction. The only texture is downstream of the phish — a small probe amount followed within minutes by a larger purchase, often at digital-goods, gift-card, gaming or travel MCCs, sometimes split across two or three merchants to stay under per-transaction limits. Ship-to and IP geography diverge from the cardholder's normal footprint, but the authentication result argues against declining.
attacks.behavioral_signature: A previously stable card suddenly transacts from a device and browser fingerprint never seen on the account, with no prior merchant relationship; the cardholder's own session activity (mobile banking, merchant app) is absent during the purchase window. Where card-on-file tokenization is attempted, a provisioning event appears on an unfamiliar device shortly after an OTP delivery that the customer later says they entered on a webpage rather than an app.
observable_signals: OTP-to-authorization latency under a few tens of seconds on a first-time merchant/device pair
brand-new device fingerprint with correct PAN, CVV and expiry on first attempt (no fumbling)
small probe authorization followed by a materially larger one at a different merchant within minutes
newly registered or recently reputation-flipped merchant domain in the acquirer referrer chain
cardholder's own app session absent or on a different IP during the OTP window
token provisioning request on an unrecognized wallet device following a web OTP delivery
post_transaction_signals: cardholder-reported fraud dispute despite a successful 3DS authentication, forcing liability argument
clustered chargebacks against one or two merchants sharing a recently onboarded payment aggregator sub-merchant ID
rapid refund-to-different-instrument requests at the receiving merchant
phishing-site takedown reports naming the same brand within the same week
attacks.real_world_grounding: Phishing with real-time OTP relay is a long-documented pattern across Indian issuers and globally; what is new and well evidenced since 2023 is the collapse in cost of per-victim personalization and fluent local-language copy, which measurably raises click-through and completion rates.
attacks.ethical_notes: Describes only the defender-visible consequences — authentication and authorization telemetry, dispute patterns — and contains no lure content, infrastructure detail, or relay technique.

attacks.name: Generative Smishing Fleets With Continuous Variant Churn
attacks.attacker_objective: Drive very large volumes of recipients into a payment or credential-capture flow — a UPI collect approval, a small 'verification' payment, an autopay mandate, or a card entry page — at whatever conversion rate volume allows.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Generative models produce effectively unlimited semantically equivalent message variants and matching landing-page text, so every recipient can receive a lexically distinct message. That removes the repetition that telecom-grade SMS filters, WhatsApp spam heuristics and DLT template controls were built to catch, and lets campaigns rotate themes — KYC expiry, electricity disconnection, parcel redelivery, reward redemption — as fast as each theme is publicised as a scam. Defenders see the same intent expressed thousands of ways rather than one template repeated.
attacks.transaction_signature: Payment-stream footprint is weak at the individual level and only visible in aggregate: many unrelated payers, each making one small-to-moderate payment (typically low hundreds to a few thousand rupees, sized under mandate and per-transaction friction thresholds) into a shrinking set of receiving VPAs, wallet handles or PA sub-merchant accounts. Card variants show low-value CNP charges at newly onboarded digital-goods merchants. Nothing about any single authorization is anomalous; the anomaly lives in the beneficiary-side fan-in and in the payer population's lack of any prior relationship with the payee.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Receiving accounts show a sharp inbound fan-in from geographically dispersed, never-before-seen payers within hours of creation or reactivation, immediately followed by outbound fan-out to further accounts. On the payer side, the account behaves normally before and after; the only account-level trace is a single first-ever payment to a payee with no contact history, frequently approved from a notification rather than initiated in-app.
observable_signals: beneficiary fan-in ratio spike: many distinct first-time payers per receiving handle within a short window
collect-request approval rate anomalies on accounts that normally only push payments
payer-to-payee first-contact-to-payment latency under a minute
cluster of payers who all received an inbound message from the same shortcode or OTT sender class
receiving VPAs or sub-merchant IDs less than 72 hours old at time of first credit
same-day outbound sweep leaving near-zero balance on the receiving account
post_transaction_signals: concentrated cybercrime-helpline and chargeback complaints naming a common receiving handle days later
recall or hold requests arriving after funds have already been layered two hops out
mule account closure requests and KYC-fraud flags on the receiving side
merchant-side refund abuse or unusually high dispute ratio on a young sub-merchant
attacks.real_world_grounding: Smishing is among the highest-volume reported fraud vectors in India and is well documented by law-enforcement and NPCI-side beneficiary analysis; generative text is a scaling and filter-evasion multiplier on an established pattern rather than a new attack class.
attacks.ethical_notes: Confines itself to aggregate beneficiary-side and messaging-volume signals that defenders already monitor, with no message content, sender infrastructure, or filter-evasion methodology.

attacks.name: Voice-Cloned Issuer And Regulator Impersonation Vishing
attacks.attacker_objective: Persuade the cardholder or account holder to disclose an authentication factor, approve a payment, or move funds to an attacker-controlled 'safe' account while believing they are speaking to their bank, card issuer, or a regulator.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Short public audio samples are enough to synthesize a convincing voice, including of a named relative or a specific bank officer the victim has previously spoken to, and streaming synthesis makes the cloned voice usable in an interactive call rather than a recording. Combined with synthetic call-centre ambience and locally accurate accent and register, this removes the auditory cues — foreign accent, stilted delivery, obvious script — that consumers were taught to treat as red flags. For defenders, the consequence is that voice familiarity, historically a strong trust signal, is no longer evidence of identity.
kill_chain: pretext call with spoofed or plausible caller identity
authentication-factor or approval extraction under urgency
attacks.transaction_signature: Payment-stream footprint is weak because the transaction is usually genuinely authorized by the customer on their own device: a correctly PIN-authenticated UPI push, a correctly OTP-authenticated card payment, or an IMPS/NEFT transfer to a newly added beneficiary. The distinguishing texture is temporal and structural, not authentication-based — a first-ever payment to a brand-new beneficiary, often at or just under a per-transaction cap, followed by repeat transfers in quick succession as the caller escalates the story, sometimes after a limit-increase or beneficiary-cooling-period change made minutes earlier.
attacks.behavioral_signature: The customer's session shows an unusually long continuous foreground presence in the banking app with long pauses between steps, indicative of being talked through the flow. Security-relevant settings changes (transaction limit raised, new beneficiary added, alerts contact changed) cluster in the same session as the first transfer. Concurrent live telephony to the customer's registered mobile is a strong contextual signal where the bank has visibility into it.
observable_signals: beneficiary added and paid within the same session with no cooling-off interval
transaction or per-day limit increased minutes before a large transfer
abnormally long dwell time between screens versus the customer's own historical pacing
multiple sequential transfers of escalating value to the same or related new beneficiaries
step-up challenges answered correctly but slowly and on the first attempt each time
customer on an active inbound call during the payment window where telco or app signal is available
post_transaction_signals: customer repudiation within hours despite valid PIN/OTP authentication, opening an authorized-push-payment dispute
recall attempt failing because funds were withdrawn or layered within minutes
receiving account showing the same-day inbound pattern from several unrelated victims
helpline complaint narrative citing a named bank officer or regulator identity
attacks.real_world_grounding: Bank-impersonation vishing and 'safe account' transfers are long documented in India and the UK; voice cloning in live calls is now credibly evidenced in family-emergency and executive-impersonation cases, and its migration into routine issuer impersonation is a near-term extrapolation already reported anecdotally by banks.
attacks.ethical_notes: Describes only the account-behaviour and dispute consequences a fraud team can act on; it names no cloning tools, sample sources, caller-ID techniques, or scripts.

attacks.name: Search- And Ad-Seeded Fake Support Desks With Always-On AI Agents
attacks.attacker_objective: Get the victim to make contact voluntarily and then extract card or account credentials, a 'verification' payment, or device access under the guise of resolving the victim's own support issue.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Generative models let a fake support presence be stood up wholesale — brand-consistent help-centre pages, plausible policy text, and a chat agent that answers arbitrary customer questions convincingly in the victim's language, around the clock and in parallel across many victims. Because the operation no longer needs staffed human agents to seem real, it can be seeded broadly across search results, marketplace listings, app-store clones, and social replies to public complaints. The critical defender consequence is trust inversion: the victim initiated contact, so every 'never trust an inbound caller' heuristic and every inbound-call detection signal is inert.
kill_chain: poisoned discovery surfaces and complaint-reply seeding
AI agent triage and trust building
attacks.transaction_signature: Payment-stream footprint is weak and often benign-looking: either a small 'refundable verification' or 'service charge' payment that the victim genuinely authorizes to an unrelated payee, or an ordinary CNP authorization on a card whose details were just re-entered. Where remote access is involved, the transactions originate from the victim's own device and IP, so device-reputation and geolocation checks pass cleanly. Amounts are typically modest at first, escalating only if the interaction continues; MCC is unremarkable or maps to generic services and digital goods.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Sessions show hallmarks of guided or remote-controlled operation — screen-sharing or remote-access applications running concurrently, unnatural input timing, navigation that goes directly to transfer or card-management screens without the customer's usual browsing. The account frequently shows a recent genuine problem (failed delivery, declined transaction, wallet balance issue) that plausibly motivated the search for support.
observable_signals: remote-access or screen-share application detected alongside an active banking or checkout session
input cadence inconsistent with the customer's historical behavioural biometric profile
payment or card re-entry occurring shortly after a failed transaction or logged support-worthy incident
navigation straight to sensitive screens with zero exploratory browsing
victim device and IP normal while payee is entirely new and unrelated to the brand in question
brand-abuse telemetry: lookalike support domains, cloned apps, or ad placements surfacing for support queries
post_transaction_signals: customer complaint stating they contacted support found via search or an app store
chargebacks or disputes referencing a 'refund' or 'verification charge' that was never reversed
subsequent unauthorized activity from the same session where device access persisted
takedown volume for lookalike support pages and cloned apps of the same brand
attacks.real_world_grounding: Fake customer-care numbers seeded into search results and business listings are a heavily reported Indian fraud pattern, and brand-cloned support chat plus fraudulent ad placement are documented globally; the always-on AI agent layer removes the staffing constraint that previously limited scale.
attacks.ethical_notes: Restricted to session, device and brand-abuse signals available to defenders; it does not explain how discovery surfaces are manipulated or how support personas are constructed.

attacks.name: Persona-Driven Romance And Investment Grooming Pipelines
attacks.attacker_objective: Build sustained emotional or financial trust over weeks so the victim voluntarily and repeatedly funds an attacker-controlled 'investment', 'trading account', or personal emergency, with escalating amounts.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Generative models sustain a consistent synthetic persona — coherent backstory, matching imagery, on-demand video or voice proof-of-life, and daily conversational continuity — across many victims simultaneously, removing the human-hours ceiling that previously limited how many long-cycle relationships one operation could maintain. They also generate the supporting fiction: dashboards showing paper gains, statements, and confident answers to financial questions. Defenders therefore see far more victims per operator, and grooming quality that no longer degrades with scale.
kill_chain: persona seeding on social and dating surfaces
small successful test withdrawal to prove legitimacy
withdrawal blocked behind fees and taxes
attacks.transaction_signature: Payment-stream footprint is weak per transaction and only meaningful as a trajectory: a slowly escalating series of victim-authorized outbound payments over weeks or months, starting small and growing by multiples, with one early small inbound credit that mimics a successful withdrawal. Destinations drift over time — first an individual account or wallet, later money-transfer, quasi-cash or crypto-adjacent merchant categories, and often a card-funded purchase of crypto or vouchers late in the cycle. Each individual payment is well within the victim's capacity; the aggregate frequently is not, ending in loan or credit-line drawdown.
attacks.behavioral_signature: The account's payment profile changes character over weeks: new recurring outbound relationships, rising ticket sizes, fixed deposits liquidated, gold or mutual-fund holdings redeemed, and personal or top-up loans taken shortly before a large transfer. Login and messaging activity concentrates in unusual hours. Victims frequently deny or minimise the relationship when contacted, which is itself a recognised indicator.
observable_signals: escalating outbound payment ladder to a rotating set of new payees over weeks
one small inbound credit early in the sequence followed by much larger outbound flows
liquidation of savings instruments or new unsecured credit immediately preceding a transfer
shift in destination mix toward money-transfer, quasi-cash and crypto-adjacent categories
customer overrides or dismisses in-app scam warnings repeatedly within the same session
denial or evasive answers during a bank intervention call about the payment purpose
post_transaction_signals: victim reports total loss only after a withdrawal is refused behind fee and tax demands
beneficiary network resolves to layered mule accounts and off-ramp services on investigation
recall impossible because funds exited to crypto or cross-border corridors within hours
clustered complaints naming the same fake trading platform brand
attacks.real_world_grounding: So-called pig-butchering fraud is extensively documented by Indian law enforcement, INTERPOL and US agencies, including industrialised operations in Southeast Asia; generative personas and content are a documented force multiplier on an established and already enormous loss category.
attacks.ethical_notes: Describes the longitudinal account trajectory and intervention failure modes banks must detect, with no persona-building, platform, or grooming methodology.

attacks.name: Code-Mixed Hinglish And Vernacular Persuasion At Population Scale
attacks.attacker_objective: Reach and convert victim segments previously insulated by language — regional-language, code-mixing and low-English-literacy users — into authorizing UPI payments, approving collect requests, or granting mandates.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Models now produce fluent Hinglish and Indic-language content, including Roman-script code-mixing, regionally correct honorifics, and the register of a genuine government or bank notification, and can do so in twenty-plus languages without a native-speaking operator. Voice synthesis extends the same fluency to calls in regional accents. The defensive consequence is asymmetric: fraud content quality in vernacular languages has jumped, while most content-classification, keyword-blocking and consumer-awareness material remains English-centric and script-normalised, so detection coverage is weakest exactly where the new volume lands.
kill_chain: code-mixed lure or call in the victim's language
trust via institutional register and local framing
victim-authorized UPI payment or mandate approval
attacks.transaction_signature: Payment-stream footprint is weak and structurally identical to ordinary low-value UPI activity: correctly PIN-authorized push payments or approved collect requests of a few hundred to a few thousand rupees, plus autopay mandate approvals that later debit recurrently. Nothing in amount, MCC or channel is distinctive. The only aggregate texture is a beneficiary-side concentration of payers sharing a regional and demographic profile, and a higher-than-normal rate of pull-request approvals among customers whose accounts otherwise show only push behaviour.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Affected accounts skew toward newer digital-payment users, older customers, and tier-2/3 and rural geographies, often with recent first-time app onboarding. Interaction shows low navigational confidence — repeated screen backtracking, help-screen visits, long dwell on the PIN prompt — and warning banners rendered in English being dismissed without dwell time, indicating they were not read.
observable_signals: collect-request approvals on accounts with a history of push-only behaviour
scam-warning screens dismissed with dwell time too short to have been read, especially in English-only locales
first-ever autopay mandate approved within minutes of an inbound message or call
beneficiary fan-in concentrated within one linguistic or regional payer cohort
recently onboarded or low-tenure digital-payment users over-represented among payers to one handle
complaint narratives and helpline transcripts arriving predominantly in one regional language
post_transaction_signals: regional clustering of authorized-payment complaints against a common beneficiary
recurring mandate debits disputed weeks later once the victim notices the standing instruction
mule accounts opened in the same district as the victim cohort, complicating cross-border assumptions
low recall success because the victim reports late relative to sweep timing
attacks.real_world_grounding: India's payment growth is overwhelmingly in vernacular-first, newly digital cohorts, and regional-language fraud is a recognised enforcement concern; the credible new element is that fluent multilingual generation removes the operator-language constraint that previously bounded such campaigns.
attacks.ethical_notes: Reports only demographic, warning-interaction and beneficiary-concentration signals a defender can measure, without any lure text, translation guidance, or targeting methodology.

attacks.name: Real-Time Adaptive Objection Handling During Live Social-Engineering Calls
attacks.attacker_objective: Keep a hesitant victim inside the payment flow by defeating each doubt as it is raised — including the bank's own warnings and interdiction call — until the transfer completes.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Live transcription plus a language model turns an unscripted call into a guided one: the caller receives continuously updated framing tuned to the specific objection the victim just voiced, including how to reinterpret the exact scam-warning text the victim is reading aloud from their screen. This converts what used to be a scripted call that collapsed on the first unanticipated question into an adaptive conversation, and it directly attacks the bank's last line of defence — in-app warnings and human interdiction — by pre-arming the victim to answer branch or call-centre questions in a way that clears the check.
attacks.transaction_signature: Payment-stream footprint is weak: the completed transaction is fully authenticated and customer-initiated, indistinguishable in the auth message from any legitimate transfer. Its distinguishing shape is the run-up rather than the record — repeated abandoned or failed attempts at the same or descending amounts, a value later split into tranches after a threshold warning fired, and completion only after several minutes of stalled interaction. Where a first attempt is declined, the retry often arrives at a slightly lower amount or via a different rail (card to UPI, or UPI to IMPS) within the same session.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Session telemetry shows a distinctive struggle-then-succeed pattern: warning screens dwelt on for a long time and then dismissed, payment flow entered and exited two or three times, help content opened, and typing cadence that alternates between long pauses and rapid bursts as the victim is coached. If an interdiction call occurs, the customer's answers are unusually rehearsed, consistent, and rushed toward ending the call.
observable_signals: multiple abandoned payment attempts followed by a successful one within a single session
long dwell on a scam-warning screen followed by dismissal and immediate completion
amount split into tranches just below the threshold that triggered a warning or step-up
rail switching after a decline within minutes for the same effective beneficiary
behavioural-biometric drift from the customer's baseline (pause structure, correction rate)
interdiction call where the customer resists questions or gives an implausibly tidy payment reason
post_transaction_signals: customer repudiation despite documented warning acknowledgement, escalating liability disputes
interdiction-effectiveness metrics degrading: warned-then-proceeded rate rising for a beneficiary cohort
recall failure due to sub-minute sweep at the beneficiary
post-incident interview revealing the victim was coached on how to answer the bank
attacks.real_world_grounding: Coached victims defeating bank interdiction is a documented and rising problem in UK and Indian authorized-payment fraud; real-time model-assisted objection handling is a credible near-term extrapolation already visible in the quality and adaptability of reported call transcripts.
attacks.ethical_notes: Safe to publish because it is framed entirely around warning-interaction and retry telemetry that defenders should instrument, and deliberately contains no persuasion content, objection responses, or interdiction-defeating language.

attacks.name: Breach-Matched Pretexting With Verifiably Accurate Personal Details
attacks.subcategory: Data-driven pretext construction and victim selection
attacks.attacker_objective: Establish immediate credibility by opening with details only a legitimate institution should know, and use that credibility to obtain an authentication factor, a payment, or a beneficiary change.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Models make it cheap to fuse messy leaked datasets — merchant order histories, loan and insurance records, delivery manifests, telecom and utility data — into per-person dossiers and to choose the right pretext, product, language and moment for each target, such as approaching someone in the narrow window after a real cash-on-delivery order or a filed claim. The persuasion value comes from accuracy rather than volume: the opening line contains a genuine order ID, correct card last four, or real policy number. For defenders this shifts the problem upstream — the decisive variable is third-party data exposure, which the bank neither controls nor sees.
attacks.transaction_signature: Payment-stream footprint is weak, and weaker than comparable untargeted scams because the victim complies quickly and without hesitation, removing the abandon-and-retry texture that hesitation normally produces. Outcomes vary by pretext: a correctly OTP-authenticated CNP charge, a small 'confirmation' UPI payment, or a first-ever transfer to a new beneficiary. Values are often deliberately matched to a real pending order or refund amount, so they look contextually reasonable and evade amount-anomaly rules.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Compliance is fast and clean — short session, no help-screen visits, minimal warning dwell — which paradoxically makes the session look more legitimate than a genuine hesitant customer's. Across a portfolio, victims cluster by a shared third party: the same merchant, insurer, lender, delivery network or app, with the incident timing tracking that third party's customer events rather than any bank-side event.
observable_signals: victim cohort sharing a common recent merchant, insurer, lender or logistics relationship
fraud reports where the complainant confirms the caller knew accurate order, policy or card-last-four details
payment amount closely matching a real pending order, refund or premium value
abnormally low hesitation metrics: short session, no warning dwell, first-attempt success
temporal clustering of incidents shortly after a third party's known or suspected data exposure
beneficiary or card-detail entry with no exploratory navigation whatsoever
post_transaction_signals: dispute narratives converging on one third party, supporting a breach-attribution investigation
issuer-level cohort analysis linking compromised cardholders to a common merchant or aggregator
elevated and sustained fraud rate on one BIN-merchant pairing after a data-exposure event
mule accounts receiving amounts that mirror legitimate order values across unrelated victims
attacks.real_world_grounding: Pretexting from leaked merchant and delivery data is a well-documented Indian pattern, notably in cash-on-delivery and loan-app contexts, and cohort-based breach attribution is standard issuer practice; the genuinely newer element is cheap fusion of heterogeneous leaked datasets into targeting and timing decisions.
attacks.ethical_notes: Publishes only the cohort-attribution and low-hesitation telemetry that fraud teams use to find a common point of exposure, with no reference to data sources, enrichment methods, or pretext content.

attacks.name: Agentically Orchestrated Credential Stuffing Into Card-On-File Cash-Out
attacks.attacker_objective: Gain authenticated control of merchant, wallet and issuer-portal accounts holding stored card credentials, then monetise the stored instrument without ever possessing the physical card.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Generative models act as an orchestration layer over breach corpora: they cluster credential material by likely mutation family per user cohort, prioritise which pairs to try against which merchant, and re-plan the attempt schedule from response semantics rather than following a fixed script. The same models produce heterogeneous session pacing and form-interaction timing profiles so attempts resemble a diverse human population instead of one tool. Defender consequence: the classic high-volume, low-variance stuffing burst fragments into many low-rate, high-diversity streams with a materially higher hit rate per attempt.
attacks.transaction_signature: Post-takeover authorisations use a legitimately stored PAN or network token, so the credential itself is clean. Typical footprint is card-on-file CNP with no CVV, a first small probe auth under INR 200 followed within minutes by higher-value spend, MCC drift toward digital goods, gift cards, gaming top-ups and travel (5815/5816/5732/4722), shipping or delivery address changed in the same session, and clustering of many unrelated accounts hitting the same small merchant set inside one window.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Account shows a hard dormant-to-active jump: login from an unrecognised device and ASN, immediate navigation straight to payment or address settings with no browse behaviour, notification-preference or e-mail change, and session length far below that account's historical median. Across the portfolio, thousands of accounts show near-identical settings-change sequences with individually plausible but collectively identical page-transition graphs.
observable_signals: login success rate per ASN deviating sharply from that ASN's historical baseline
new device fingerprint plus new ASN plus zero prior cookie history on a mature account
time-from-login to payment-settings edit far below account median
contact-channel change (email, phone, notification opt-out) preceding first auth
reuse of one device or canvas fingerprint hash across unrelated customer IDs
first post-login auth is a low-value probe followed by escalation in the same session
post_transaction_signals: fraud chargebacks under card-absent liability once the true cardholder notices
victim complaint that account e-mail was silently changed
concentration of disputes against a narrow merchant set fed by many issuers
digital-goods resale or gift-card redemption traced to a shared redemption pool
attacks.real_world_grounding: Credential stuffing against Indian e-commerce, OTT and wallet accounts is routinely reported and underpins a large share of card-on-file CNP fraud; the AI contribution is throughput, per-target prioritisation and behavioural diversity rather than a new mechanism.
attacks.ethical_notes: Describes only portfolio-level detection surfaces and post-takeover consequences; contains no credential sources, tooling, proxy strategy or evasion configuration.

attacks.name: On-Device Malware Session Hijack Preserving The Victim's Trusted Device Fingerprint
attacks.attacker_objective: Transact from inside the victim's own authenticated banking or UPI session on the victim's own handset, so every device-binding, SIM-binding and fingerprint check passes truthfully.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Generative models are used upstream to mass-produce convincing localised lures and app clones, and downstream to parse the victim's on-screen financial state and select the highest-yield action and timing per victim rather than draining uniformly. This turns a blunt overlay trojan into a per-victim decision agent that picks amounts, beneficiaries and hours consistent with that account's own history. Defensive consequence: fraud arrives with a genuine device fingerprint, genuine device binding and per-victim-tuned amounts, stripping away the anomaly features most ATO models depend on.
attacks.transaction_signature: Authorisations originate from the correctly bound device with valid app attestation and the registered SIM, so device and geo features look normal. The tell is transaction shape: a sequence of transfers just under the customer's own step-up threshold, UPI P2P or A2A pushes to first-seen VPAs and newly added beneficiaries, execution concentrated in low-attention hours (roughly 01:00-05:00 IST), and total drain approaching available balance or full card limit within one to three hours.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Screen-interaction telemetry diverges from the enrolled human even though hardware identifiers do not: accessibility-driven input with no touch pressure or gyroscope variance, near-zero typing entropy, impossible navigation speed between screens, no natural idle gaps. Beneficiary additions and limit increases occur inside the same session as the transfers, and SMS or notification permissions were altered shortly before.
observable_signals: input events without corresponding accelerometer or touch-pressure variance
accessibility service or screen-overlay flag newly enabled on a long-lived device
app-session navigation timings orders of magnitude faster than the account baseline
multiple first-seen beneficiaries or VPAs added minutes before first debit
cluster of unrelated customers pushing funds to the same beneficiary in one window
SMS-read or notification-access permission change immediately preceding activity
post_transaction_signals: victim disputes filed hours later after they regain phone attention
beneficiary account emptied through layered UPI hops or ATM withdrawal within minutes
recall requests failing because funds already moved through two or more mule layers
multiple victim reports converging on one sideloaded application name
attacks.real_world_grounding: Accessibility-abusing Android banking trojans targeting Indian UPI and net-banking apps are extensively documented by CERT-In and mobile-security vendors; the generative element is lure quality at scale and per-victim amount selection, not the malware capability itself.
attacks.ethical_notes: Frames the attack purely as behavioural-telemetry divergence on a trusted device; no malware technique, permission-abuse method or distribution channel is described.

attacks.name: MFA Fatigue Push-Bombing With A Synchronised Support Pretext
attacks.attacker_objective: Convert a stolen password or partially compromised account into a fully approved authentication by inducing the victim to approve a push prompt they believe is a routine security action.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Language models generate the accompanying support pretext in the victim's language and register, timed to arrive alongside the push storm and referencing plausible account specifics so the approval feels like the resolution to the annoyance rather than its cause. The same models tune prompt cadence and follow-up wording per victim segment and produce a fallback narrative after a decline. The defender-visible result is that approval-after-decline-burst, previously a strong fraud indicator, now co-occurs with a legitimate-looking supporting contact and a shorter, less obviously abusive prompt series.
attacks.transaction_signature: Transactions carry a fully approved strong-authentication result, so the authorisation stream looks compliant. The distinguishing footprint is what follows enrolment: a new trusted device added, then near-immediate outbound A2A or UPI transfers to new beneficiaries or high-value CNP spend, typically within the same hour and often exhausting a large share of the daily transfer limit.
attacks.behavioral_signature: A burst of authentication challenges with several denials or timeouts, then a single approval, followed by device enrolment from an ASN and geography the account has never used. The victim's legitimate device continues normal usage in parallel, producing two concurrently active trusted sessions. Historically the victim rarely denies prompts, making the denial burst itself anomalous relative to their own baseline.
observable_signals: three or more denied or expired push challenges preceding one approval
approval originating from a session whose IP or ASN differs from the approving handset's network
new trusted-device enrolment within minutes of the approval
concurrent active sessions from geographically inconsistent locations
inbound support-channel contact recorded in the same window as the prompt series
beneficiary addition immediately after enrolment on an account with a stable beneficiary list
post_transaction_signals: victim reports never intending to authorise the transfer
funds layered through mule accounts before the victim's first complaint
dispute resolution complicated by a compliant strong-authentication record
repeat targeting of the same victim after the first successful approval
attacks.real_world_grounding: Push-bombing combined with a helpdesk pretext is a documented technique behind several large enterprise and consumer account compromises; generative language models mainly lower the cost of producing fluent, localised pretexts at volume.
attacks.ethical_notes: Limits itself to the challenge-response pattern defenders can monitor; no pretext wording, cadence parameters or targeting method is supplied.

attacks.name: SIM-Swap-Assisted Takeover Of SMS-Bound Financial Identity
attacks.attacker_objective: Seize control of the victim's mobile number so that all SMS-delivered codes, UPI device-binding SMS and recovery flows resolve to attacker-held hardware.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Generative tooling supports the telecom-side impersonation: synthesised voice consistent with the subscriber profile, and identity artefacts consistent with aggregated open-source data about that subscriber. Language models assemble a coherent per-victim dossier from scattered public and breached fragments so the interaction survives challenge questions. The defender-relevant consequence is a higher success rate per porting attempt and a compressed window between reconnaissance and port.
kill_chain: victim profiling from open and breached data
carrier-side impersonation and port or replacement
control of SMS and device-binding channel
attacks.transaction_signature: Once re-bound, transactions are technically well-formed and pass SMS-based checks: UPI re-registration from a new handset followed by transfers to new VPAs, card re-issue or token provisioning, and high-value A2A pushes. Amounts frequently sit at or just below per-transaction caps and repeat until daily limits are exhausted; activity is compressed into a short window because the attacker expects the victim to notice loss of signal.
attacks.behavioral_signature: The account exhibits a hard identity discontinuity: SIM or IMSI change event, new device binding, multiple password and recovery-channel resets across banking, wallet and e-mail within a compressed window, and every subsequent action from a device with zero history. The victim's prior device stops appearing entirely rather than continuing in parallel.
observable_signals: SIM change or IMSI change flag within the issuer's cooling-off window
UPI device re-binding on a handset with no prior relationship to the customer
credential and recovery-channel resets across multiple institutions in the same hour
complete disappearance of the previously dominant device fingerprint
high-value transfers immediately after re-binding on an account with a low-value baseline
port-out or replacement request geography inconsistent with the customer's usual circle
post_transaction_signals: victim reports loss of mobile network preceding the fraud
cross-institution reports converging on one customer identity
mule beneficiary accounts drained through layered hops within minutes
carrier-side port record contradicting the customer's own account of events
attacks.real_world_grounding: SIM swap is a long-established and heavily litigated fraud vector in India and globally, which is why regulators mandate cooling-off periods on SIM change before certain transactions; voice cloning and AI-assembled dossiers are an incremental, credible accelerant to the impersonation step.
attacks.ethical_notes: Describes only the cross-institution discontinuity signals defenders already correlate; contains no carrier-process detail, impersonation script or porting method.

attacks.name: Synthetic Identity Cultivation With Machine-Generated Digital Footprints
attacks.attacker_objective: Establish a durable non-existent customer with a credible history, mature it through normal-looking behaviour, and convert accumulated credit and transfer limits into an uncollectable loss.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Generative models manufacture the connective tissue that bureau and KYC checks implicitly test for: internally consistent biographies, plausible employment and address chronology, portrait imagery with no prior existence on the open web, and a thin but coherent social and e-commerce trail cultivated over months. Agentic tooling maintains hundreds of such personas in parallel, each with distinct behavioural cadence, so they do not correlate with one another. The consequence is that the sparse-file heuristics defenders rely on to flag synthetics are satisfied by genuine, if manufactured, activity.
kill_chain: thin-file onboarding at a tolerant institution
attacks.transaction_signature: For most of its life the identity generates deliberately unremarkable authorisations: small recurring MCCs, utility and telecom payments, on-time repayments, gradual ticket-size growth. The bust-out phase inverts this abruptly with near-simultaneous maximum-utilisation spend across every open line, cash-equivalent and quasi-cash MCCs, gift-card and jewellery purchases, and large outbound A2A transfers, followed by total silence and no repayment.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Identity has no pre-onboarding history anywhere and no relatives, co-applicants or shared-address links to established identities. Contact details are digital-only and recently created. Over time subtle infrastructure sharing emerges across supposedly unrelated identities: overlapping device attributes, address-normalisation collisions, near-identical session cadence, and coordinated application timing across institutions.
observable_signals: portrait image with no reverse-image or prior-web presence and near-perfect framing consistency
identity attributes whose earliest observable date postdates the claimed age by decades
many first-time applicants sharing device, ASN or address-normalisation clusters
credit-line utilisation trajectory that is smooth then abruptly maximal
application velocity across multiple institutions inside a narrow window
behavioural cadence across supposedly unrelated customers with abnormally low variance
post_transaction_signals: first-party or never-pay default with no traceable person behind the account
collections contact failing entirely across every supplied channel
bureau reconstruction revealing a cluster of identities that matured in lockstep
losses booked as credit charge-off rather than fraud, hiding true attribution
attacks.real_world_grounding: Synthetic identity fraud is the fastest-growing loss category in several mature credit markets and is well documented in bust-out form; generative imagery and agentic footprint cultivation materially raise the realism and parallelism of what was previously a slow, manual craft.
attacks.ethical_notes: Presents only lifecycle and portfolio-correlation signals used by credit and fraud teams; supplies no synthesis method, document specification or onboarding-evasion guidance.

attacks.name: Generated Supporting Documents And Manipulated Identity Artefacts At Verification
attacks.attacker_objective: Pass document-based identity, address and income verification using artefacts that are internally coherent and visually clean but correspond to no genuine issued record.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Image and layout models produce or alter identity and supporting artefacts (statements, payslips, utility bills, address proofs) that are typographically consistent, arithmetically self-consistent and free of the crude splice artefacts earlier forgery detection targeted. Language models generate the accompanying narrative so the applicant's stated history matches every field across a multi-document bundle. The defender-visible shift is that inconsistency-based document checks lose signal while provenance-based checks (issuer validation, metadata, capture forensics) become the only reliable discriminator.
attacks.transaction_signature: No distinctive authorisation footprint exists at onboarding — the fraud completes before any transaction. Downstream the account behaves either as a bust-out credit line or, more commonly in India, as a funnel account receiving many small inbound UPI and A2A credits from unrelated remitters and pushing them onward within minutes, with almost no genuine consumption spend.
attacks.behavioral_signature: The documented persona and the operational behaviour never converge: a stated salaried professional whose account shows no salary credit, an address that never receives a card delivery, a customer who never uses any non-payment feature. Verification imagery shows unnatural capture uniformity across documents that should have different physical provenance.
observable_signals: absent or synthetic capture metadata and recompression traces inconsistent with a phone camera
identical lighting, crop geometry or noise profile across documents of different claimed origin
document fields arithmetically perfect in a way real statements rarely are
issuer or registry validation failing or unavailable while the artefact itself looks clean
the same address or employer string recurring across unrelated applicants after normalisation
no salary or income credit appearing in an account onboarded on income documents
post_transaction_signals: account rapidly reclassified as a mule after inbound victim complaints
card or welcome kit undeliverable at the verified address
charge-off with no traceable person and no enforceable contact
law-enforcement notice tying the account to unrelated victim losses
attacks.real_world_grounding: Forged KYC and income documentation is long established in Indian lending and mule-account creation; generative image and layout models have demonstrably raised artefact quality, shifting practical detection from visual inconsistency toward issuer-side and forensic provenance validation.
attacks.ethical_notes: Discusses only forensic and provenance signals used by verification teams; omits any description of how artefacts are produced or which checks are weakest.

attacks.name: Deepfake Liveness And Video-KYC Defeat At Remote Onboarding
attacks.attacker_objective: Clear a live biometric or video-KYC check with a synthetic or puppeteered face so a fabricated or stolen identity is bound to an account under a regulator-recognised verification.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Real-time face synthesis and reenactment can sustain a responsive human likeness through an interactive session, including head turns, expression changes and lip-synced speech in the expected language, presented through a virtual capture path rather than held to a screen. Audio synthesis keeps voice and face consistent under questioning. The defender consequence is that challenge-response liveness, which assumed a synthetic could not react in real time, degrades into a passable test, pushing detection toward stream-provenance and hardware-attestation signals.
attacks.transaction_signature: Produces no authorisation footprint at the moment of attack. The onboarded account subsequently shows one of two shapes: a mule funnel with rapid inbound-then-outbound UPI and A2A churn across many unrelated counterparties, or a credit line matured briefly then maximised across cash-equivalent MCCs and abandoned.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Session-layer telemetry contradicts the apparent human: virtual or non-attested camera device, frame timing too regular for handheld capture, absent sensor fusion (no gyroscope or accelerometer motion correlated with visible head movement), and challenge-reaction latency that is implausibly uniform or slightly lagged. The same underlying likeness or capture environment recurs across nominally different applicants.
observable_signals: virtual camera or non-attested capture path detected during the session
frame-rate and inter-frame timing regularity inconsistent with handheld video
no correlation between visible head motion and device motion sensors
face embedding matching a prior enrolment under a different identity
challenge-response latency variance abnormally low across the session
facial-region rendering artefacts at occlusion boundaries under motion
post_transaction_signals: account flagged as mule after downstream victim complaints
biometric duplicate detected against later enrolments in the same portfolio
enrolled person unreachable or denies ever holding the account
regulatory audit finding a verified-KYC account with no real customer behind it
attacks.real_world_grounding: Injection attacks against remote biometric onboarding are documented by biometric-testing bodies and have driven multiple financial-sector advisories, including Asian cases where video-KYC was cleared with synthetic likenesses; this is genuinely enabled by recent real-time generative models.
attacks.ethical_notes: Written entirely from the verifier's telemetry perspective — capture provenance, sensor correlation, rendering artefacts — with no injection technique, tooling or weakest-check guidance.

attacks.name: Aggregated-Data Knowledge-Based Authentication Defeat In Account Recovery
attacks.attacker_objective: Pass issuer or merchant identity-verification questions and human-agent recovery checks well enough to have credentials, contact details or delivery instructions reset in the attacker's favour.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Language models fuse breach corpora, public registries and social and e-commerce residue into a single per-victim dossier that anticipates the specific verification questions a given institution asks, ranking candidate answers by confidence. In a live agent call the model supplies real-time suggestions and a recovery narrative when a question is missed, so the caller never stalls. The consequence for defenders is that static and dynamic KBA both lose discriminative power, because the attacker's answer distribution now closely matches the genuine customer's.
kill_chain: asset movement or reissued instrument abuse
attacks.transaction_signature: The compromise itself is invisible in the authorisation stream. Downstream authorisations look ordinary but the instrument or delivery has been redirected: card reissued to a changed address, token provisioned to an unfamiliar wallet, or transfers to newly added beneficiaries. Ticket sizes often deliberately match the account's baseline, defeating amount-anomaly rules.
attacks.behavioral_signature: A back-office or voice-channel identity verification succeeds on an account that then immediately changes its contact channels. The customer's own digital session activity is absent throughout, and the historically dominant device continues normal behaviour afterward, unaware. Repeat verification attempts across several institutions for the same identity cluster in a short window.
observable_signals: successful KBA on a call from a number never associated with the customer
contact-detail or address change within minutes of verification passing
one or more failed verification attempts on the same identity shortly beforehand
recovery attempt occurring with no corresponding digital session from the customer's device
cross-institution verification attempts for one identity inside a narrow time window
card reissue or token provisioning immediately following the reset
post_transaction_signals: customer reports never receiving a reissued card or never requesting the reset
dispute arising weeks later once statements reach the old address
call-recording review revealing answer patterns inconsistent with the genuine customer
fraud reported concurrently at multiple institutions for the same identity
attacks.real_world_grounding: KBA has been treated as structurally weak by regulators and industry for over a decade because of breach saturation; large-scale aggregation and live answer assistance is a documented and credible extension that further collapses its residual value.
attacks.ethical_notes: Focuses on verification-channel and reset-sequence signals available to fraud operations; names no data sources, question sets or impersonation method.

attacks.name: Low-And-Slow Distributed BIN Enumeration Across Merchant Long-Tail
attacks.attacker_objective: Discover which PAN/expiry/CVV combinations within a known issuer BIN range are live and authorizable, producing a validated card inventory for later monetisation.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Agentic orchestration lets a single operator drive checkout attempts across hundreds of unrelated small merchants simultaneously, adapting to each site's flow without hand-written per-merchant scripts, so per-merchant velocity stays under any single acquirer's threshold while aggregate throughput is very high. Generative models also produce plausible, internally consistent synthetic billing identities per attempt (name, address, email, phone in matching Indian pincode/state combinations), which defeats naive duplicate-value detection because no two attempts share fields. The effect defenders see is enumeration whose statistical fingerprint is only visible at network level, not merchant level.
attacks.transaction_signature: Very high decline-to-approve ratio concentrated in contiguous or algorithmically-adjacent PAN ranges within one or a few issuer BINs; small ticket sizes (often INR 1-50 or the merchant minimum) or zero-amount account verification messages; heavy skew toward low-risk MCCs such as 5815/5816 digital goods, 8398 donations, and 5968 subscription/direct marketing; wide merchant spread with only 1-3 attempts per merchant per hour; response-code mix dominated by 'do not honour', 'invalid CVV2/expiry' rather than 'insufficient funds'.
attacks.behavioral_signature: No account tenure anywhere — each attempt originates from a session with zero history, no returning-device cookie, and no post-approval behaviour. Approved cards are immediately abandoned rather than used, producing a distinctive 'approve then silence' pattern. Attempt timing shows machine-regular inter-arrival distributions at network level even where each individual merchant sees only sporadic traffic.
observable_signals: Issuer-level decline rate spike confined to narrow PAN neighbourhoods
Same-BIN attempts fanned across many unrelated acquirers within minutes
Zero-amount / account-verification messages with no follow-on purchase
Approved low-value auth with no subsequent activity on that PAN
CVV2/expiry mismatch codes clustered by PAN prefix
Session fingerprints with no cookie age and no prior merchant history
post_transaction_signals: Validated PANs surface days later in unrelated high-value CNP fraud
Merchant misuse-of-authorisation-system fees and network enumeration-programme notices
Cardholder disputes on the tiny test charges that were never reversed
Cluster of first-fraud dates traceable to a common enumeration window
attacks.real_world_grounding: Card testing and BIN enumeration are long-documented; card networks run dedicated enumeration-monitoring programmes and issuers routinely observe attack waves against small merchants. What is newer is the ease of orchestrating heterogeneous merchant checkouts and generating unique synthetic billing data per attempt at scale.
attacks.ethical_notes: Describes the aggregate authorization-stream and behavioural footprint a defender can measure; contains no merchant targeting criteria, no evasion thresholds, and no tooling.

attacks.name: Post-Validation CNP Monetisation Through Resale-Liquid Digital Goods
attacks.attacker_objective: Convert an already-validated stolen card into resaleable value before the cardholder or issuer notices, maximising extraction per card in a short window.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Generative models let an operator produce coherent, per-card purchase personas — shipping identity, contact details, and a purchase narrative consistent with the card's issuing geography — so that address-verification and identity-consistency checks see plausible rather than templated data. Agentic browsing sustains parallel checkout sessions across many merchants at once, compressing the exploitation window between validation and issuer block. The novelty is throughput and per-attempt uniqueness, not any new payment mechanic.
attacks.transaction_signature: Burst of medium-value CNP authorisations (typically INR 2,000-25,000) within a compressed window across several merchants; strong bias toward instantly-fulfilled or resale-liquid categories — gift-card and stored-value MCC 6540/5815, gaming top-ups, digital subscriptions, travel MCC 4722 — with no shipping delay to interrupt cash-out. Billing and delivery geography frequently diverges from the card's historic authorisation footprint; currency or acquirer country may differ from issuer country. AVS/CVV2 results are often full-match because the data was validated earlier, so the classic mismatch signal is absent.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Guest checkout or brand-new merchant accounts created minutes before purchase; no browsing depth, no cart abandonment, no wishlist history — straight to checkout. Device and IP reused across multiple distinct cardholder identities within hours, which is the strongest cross-merchant tell. Spend velocity is wholly discontinuous with the card's own history.
observable_signals: Multi-merchant authorisation burst on one PAN inside a short window
One device or IP associated with many unrelated cardholder names
Merchant account age measured in minutes at time of high-value purchase
Shipping/billing mismatch or delivery to freight-forwarder and locker addresses
Sharp shift into stored-value and instantly-fulfilled MCCs
Full AVS/CVV2 match combined with zero device or account history
post_transaction_signals: Cardholder-not-authorised chargebacks (reason 10.4 / 4837 class) clustered by purchase date
Gift-card codes redeemed from geographies unrelated to purchase
Merchant fraud-to-sales ratio breach on affected MIDs
Common-point-of-purchase analysis linking many disputed PANs to one earlier breach
attacks.real_world_grounding: Classic CNP cash-out through resale-liquid digital goods is one of the best-documented fraud patterns in card networks and underpins most CNP chargeback volume. GenAI changes the speed and per-attempt data uniqueness, not the underlying economics.
attacks.ethical_notes: Frames the attack purely as authorization-stream and dispute-stream consequences that a detector can score; no merchant lists, no data-preparation guidance.

attacks.name: Digital-Wallet Provisioning Takeover Via Yellow-Path Identity Defeat
attacks.attacker_objective: Push a stolen card into a wallet on an attacker-controlled device so that subsequent spend carries device-bound token credentials and contactless/in-app trust rather than raw PAN risk.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Provisioning that fails the automatic (green) path is routed to an identification-and-verification step — a one-time passcode to the cardholder's registered channel, or a call/chat with the issuer's service desk. Generative AI attacks both branches: synthesised voice and real-time conversational coaching let an attacker sustain a convincing cardholder persona through an issuer verification call, while personalised, contextually-timed phishing content harvests the provisioning passcode by presenting it as a routine card-security confirmation. Where document upload is used, image-generation models produce plausible identity artefacts. The result for the network is a provisioning decision that looks legitimately approved.
kill_chain: ID&V challenge interception or social defeat
attacks.transaction_signature: The provisioning event itself is the primary artefact, not a purchase: a token-provisioning request whose device attestation, device model, wallet-account age, and geography are all new to the cardholder, frequently reaching the issuer within minutes of a card-data compromise or a customer-service contact. Subsequent spend arrives as device-token transactions with high assurance-level indicators — contactless CP entry mode, cryptogram present, DPAN not PAN — which historically score as LOW risk. Early spend skews to fast, resale-liquid, contactless-accepted retail and stored value.
attacks.behavioral_signature: The victim's genuine device continues normal usage while a second, previously unseen device holds an active token on the same PAN. Provisioning often follows a cluster of failed logins, a password/contact-detail change, or an inbound service-desk contact within the preceding hour. The attacker device typically provisions several unrelated cardholders' cards over time — a one-device-many-cardholders shape that is invisible to any single issuer view but stark at network level.
observable_signals: Provisioning request from device with no prior relationship to the cardholder
Token activation within minutes of an ID&V call, OTP delivery, or contact-detail change
Wallet account age far younger than cardholder tenure
Same wallet/device attestation provisioning cards for multiple unrelated cardholders
Provisioning geography inconsistent with recent genuine card-present activity
First token spend clustered in stored-value or fast-fulfilment merchants
post_transaction_signals: Cardholder disputes contactless transactions from a city or device they never used
Issuer token-lifecycle review showing an unrecognised device binding
Chargebacks on transactions carrying strong CP authentication indicators, which is itself anomalous
Service-desk recording review confirming an impersonated verification call
attacks.real_world_grounding: Wallet provisioning fraud via ID&V defeat is a well-documented and materially costly pattern for issuers, and networks publish provisioning-risk scoring specifically because of it. Voice synthesis and real-time conversational assistance are a credible and already-emerging escalation of the service-desk branch.
attacks.ethical_notes: Explains the provisioning-decision and token-spend signals available to issuers and networks; it does not describe how any verification step is structured, worded, or defeated.

attacks.name: Token Lifecycle Abuse And Laundering Of Assurance Through Trusted Tokens
attacks.attacker_objective: Obtain or retain a network/merchant token that carries elevated authentication assurance, and exploit the fact that the token keeps accruing trust signals independently of the compromise that created it.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Reasoning models make it cheap to map where token trust is conferred and where it is inherited — which token requestors carry which assurance levels, how token-assurance and cryptogram indicators flow into issuer scoring, and how a token survives events like card reissue via lifecycle updates. That mapping lets an operator prioritise obtaining tokens over raw PANs and choose spend patterns that let a young token 'season' into a trusted one. Generative tooling also sustains the low-friction, plausible early activity that builds a token's own transaction history.
attacks.transaction_signature: A DPAN whose own transaction history looks progressively better than the underlying PAN's risk warrants: rising token-assurance indicators, high proportion of authenticated (3DS/cryptogram-bearing) transactions, low decline rate, and steadily increasing ticket sizes. Critically, a token provisioned during compromise can outlive PAN reissue through automatic lifecycle update, so a card the issuer believes it has replaced continues to authorise. Escalation shows as a step-change in ticket size after weeks of small, clean, well-authenticated activity — and card-on-file tokens spreading to new merchants without a corresponding new-card-entry event.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Token usage stays anchored to one device or requestor while the genuine cardholder's own activity pattern shows no awareness of it. Merchant-token proliferation happens through account-based flows (adding the wallet as a payment method) rather than PAN entry, so it leaves no card-entry footprint. Over weeks the token accumulates repeat-merchant relationships that make it look like an established instrument.
observable_signals: Token assurance level rising without any re-verification event
Token surviving PAN reissue and immediately resuming spend on a device never seen pre-reissue
Ticket-size step-change after a sustained low-value seasoning period
One token requestor / device propagating card-on-file tokens to many merchants
High authenticated-transaction ratio on a token whose underlying PAN sits in a breached cohort
Token-to-PAN risk divergence: token scores clean, PAN cohort scores dirty
post_transaction_signals: Disputes on fully authenticated token transactions where liability has shifted to the issuer
Token lifecycle audit revealing a binding the cardholder never recognised
Post-reissue fraud on a PAN the issuer considered closed
Merchant card-on-file cleanup surfacing tokens tied to a single fraudulent requestor
attacks.real_world_grounding: Token assurance levels, lifecycle updates surviving reissue, and the liability shift on authenticated token transactions are documented properties of network tokenisation, and issuers have observed fraud persisting through reissue. The systematic 'prefer tokens over PANs and season them' strategy is a credible near-term extrapolation rather than a fully catalogued campaign type.
attacks.ethical_notes: Discusses trust-inheritance as a detection gap for issuers and networks to close; contains no information about obtaining, requesting, or manipulating tokens.

attacks.name: Weak-Checkout Endpoint Harvesting For Merchant And Instrument Enumeration
attacks.attacker_objective: Locate merchant checkout and payment-page integrations with weak server-side controls and use them as durable, low-cost validation surfaces for card and VPA credentials.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Code-capable models can read a merchant's public payment integration surface and characterise its control posture at a glance, letting an operator triage thousands of candidate merchants for weak configurations far faster than manual review. Agentic execution then adapts to each site's distinct checkout structure without bespoke engineering. For UPI, the equivalent target is a collect-request or VPA-validation surface that confirms whether an address resolves to a real account holder.
attacks.transaction_signature: Extreme attempt-to-approval asymmetry concentrated on a small number of merchant IDs, often on merchants whose legitimate volume is negligible — a low-traffic MID suddenly carrying thousands of authorisation or verification messages. Amounts are minimal or zero; many attempts never reach a purchase message at all, appearing instead as account-verification, pre-auth, or name-lookup traffic. On UPI rails the analogue is a burst of VPA-resolution or unaccepted collect requests with near-zero acceptance rate, often from a single PSP handle cohort.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Traffic to the merchant lacks the whole pre-purchase funnel — no catalogue browsing, no cart events, no session depth — arriving directly at the payment step. Requests come from rotating infrastructure with fresh fingerprints, and the same merchant surface is revisited in waves separated by quiet periods. Once a merchant hardens its controls, the pattern reappears on a structurally similar merchant within days.
observable_signals: Authorisation volume on a MID wildly disproportionate to its historic baseline
Payment-step traffic with no preceding funnel events
Near-zero approval rate sustained over thousands of attempts
Distinct PANs per attempt, distinct BINs, but common request infrastructure
Wave-and-pause timing with migration to similar merchants after remediation
UPI: high-volume VPA resolution or collect requests with negligible acceptance
post_transaction_signals: Acquirer enumeration-programme notices and network fines against the abused MID
Merchant processing-cost spike from decline volume with no revenue
Credentials validated here appearing in fraud at unrelated merchants weeks later
Cardholder complaints about unexplained verification notifications
attacks.real_world_grounding: Abuse of weakly-protected checkout and payment endpoints as free card-validation infrastructure is well documented, and both networks and acquirers run programmes that penalise merchants whose endpoints are used this way. Automated triage of integration posture at scale is the GenAI-accelerated component.
attacks.ethical_notes: Deliberately describes only the volumetric and funnel-shape signals an acquirer or network sees; it names no weakness class, no endpoint behaviour, and no discovery technique.

attacks.name: Recurring Mandate And Subscription Abuse On A Compromised Instrument
attacks.attacker_objective: Establish durable recurring debits on a compromised card, UPI autopay mandate, or bank mandate so that value extraction continues quietly long after the initial compromise.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Generative models mass-produce the connective tissue that makes a recurring debit look legitimate: distinct merchant-facing subscriber identities, plausible service branding and descriptors, and mandate-consent notifications that read like ordinary subscription confirmations rather than alarms. The same capability produces the low-friction customer-support and cancellation-deflection correspondence that keeps a victim from escalating quickly. Individually these were always possible; at scale they let one operator run many parallel recurring streams across many victims.
attacks.transaction_signature: Repeating, calendar-regular debits at modest amounts (commonly INR 99-999 in the Indian market, deliberately near the psychological ignore-threshold and, for cards, historically near or below step-up-authentication thresholds), flagged as recurring/MIT with stored-credential indicators, so per-transaction risk scoring treats them as established relationships. The first transaction in the series is the only one carrying full authentication context; every subsequent one inherits it. On UPI this appears as an autopay mandate with a modest per-debit cap and a long validity window; on A2A as a standing instruction. Merchant descriptors are often generic or rotate slightly between cycles.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Mandate creation typically coincides with an account-takeover window or a phishing/support-impersonation contact, and is frequently accompanied by contact-detail changes or notification-channel suppression so the victim's mandate-confirmation and pre-debit notifications never land. Once running, there is no session activity at all — the fraud is entirely server-side and generates zero device signal, which is precisely why it survives so long. Cancellation attempts by the victim are met with attrition rather than refusal.
observable_signals: New mandate or card-on-file registration within hours of a contact-detail or credential change
Recurring debits at an amount just under common alert or step-up thresholds
Mandate-confirmation notification bounce, suppression, or redirect to a new address
Many unrelated payers holding mandates to the same or near-identical merchant descriptor
Recurring series whose first transaction is authenticated and all others are not
Long mandate validity with high cumulative cap versus small per-debit amount
post_transaction_signals: Late bulk disputes covering many cycles once the victim finally reviews statements
Mandate revocation and recall requests clustering on one merchant within days
Elevated cancellation-complaint and grievance volume against a single descriptor
Merchant refund-to-sales ratio and dispute-latency profile far outside category norms
attacks.real_world_grounding: Subscription and mandate abuse on compromised instruments is a documented and persistent pattern; India's e-mandate framework and UPI Autopay pre-debit notification rules were introduced specifically because low-value recurring debits evade victim attention. GenAI's contribution is the cheap production of convincing merchant identities and deflection correspondence at scale.
attacks.ethical_notes: Describes the recurring-transaction and notification-suppression signals that issuers, PSPs, and mandate registries can monitor; it prescribes no mandate-setup method, threshold, or victim-handling script.

attacks.name: Thread-Aware Vendor Invoice Redirection Against SME Payables
attacks.attacker_objective: Redirect a small business's genuine, expected supplier payment to attacker-controlled bank details by altering the banking coordinates on an otherwise legitimate invoice relationship.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Where an attacker has visibility into a real supplier thread, a language model reproduces the vendor's established tone, invoice numbering conventions, and correspondence cadence closely enough that the linguistic tells SME staff are trained to spot largely disappear. Document synthesis regenerates the invoice PDF with consistent formatting, logo placement, GSTIN and PO references intact and only the beneficiary block changed. The attack is timed to a genuinely pending payable, so the request arrives when the recipient is already expecting it.
kill_chain: bank-detail change notice matched to a pending payable
attacks.transaction_signature: The amount, timing, and payment cycle are entirely normal for the business — this is the defining difficulty. The only anomaly is a changed beneficiary for a payee the business has paid repeatedly. Frequently visible as: a long-standing vendor name paired with a newly-registered account number or a beneficiary account whose name is a near-miss of the vendor's (transliteration variant, dropped suffix, 'Enterprises' vs 'Enterprise'). Often a first payment at partial value to test, then the full payable.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Vendor master record edited from a corporate banking session shortly before the payment run, sometimes outside normal hours or by a user who does not usually edit master data. No corresponding change request through the procurement system. The genuine vendor continues to chase the invoice as unpaid in a parallel channel.
observable_signals: beneficiary account changed for a payee with 6+ months of stable payment history
beneficiary name-match score below threshold against the vendor master name
vendor master edit and payment release within the same or adjacent session
new beneficiary account opened within 60 days receiving a large first credit
payment amount exactly matches a known recurring payable but to a new destination
duplicate chase for the same invoice number arriving on a different channel
post_transaction_signals: genuine supplier raises non-receipt at the next ageing cycle
recall request against a beneficiary account already emptied
receiving bank reports the account as newly onboarded with atypical credit profile
second victim business identified paying the same beneficiary account
attacks.real_world_grounding: Invoice redirection is one of the best-documented business payment frauds globally and a leading SME loss driver in India, the UK, and the EU. Confirmation-of-payee style name checking measurably reduces it, which is why beneficiary-name mismatch is the load-bearing signal here; GenAI's role is to erode the language-quality tell, not to create the pattern.
attacks.ethical_notes: Describes the payables-side control failure and the beneficiary-change signals defenders monitor, without any detail on obtaining supplier correspondence or forging documents.

attacks.name: Executive-Voice Business Email Compromise Payment Instruction
attacks.attacker_objective: Obtain a single high-value out-of-cycle corporate transfer by impersonating an executive or an executive's authority to a finance staff member.
attacks.genai_mechanism: The decisive change is that the corroboration step now fails. Finance staff are trained to verify an unusual written instruction by voice or video call-back; synthetic voice and video make that call-back a confirmation of the fraud rather than a defence against it, and there are documented multi-participant video-call cases. A language model additionally sustains the executive's register and knowledge of internal context across a back-and-forth exchange, so a hesitant employee's questions get plausible answers instead of stonewalling.
kill_chain: synthetic voice or video defeats the call-back check
attacks.transaction_signature: A single large outbound transfer, materially above the entity's typical per-payment value, to a brand-new beneficiary, released outside the normal payment run — frequently late in the day, before a weekend or a public holiday to maximise the recall gap. Often cross-border, or domestic into a current account whose name resembles a legal or advisory firm. Dual-authorisation is either bypassed by seniority pressure or satisfied by a second employee subjected to the same impersonation.
