attacks.behavioral_signature: Payment initiated by a user who rarely initiates, or approved by an approver acting outside their usual counterparty set. Instruction thread lives outside the ERP/procurement system. Compressed decision window: instruction to release in well under the organisation's median. No purchase order, no contract reference, and secrecy framing that suppresses internal checking.
observable_signals: single payment exceeding the entity's 99th-percentile transfer value
new beneficiary with zero prior relationship and no PO linkage
release timed outside the standard payment run or into a holiday window
initiator/approver pair with no prior co-approval history
cross-border destination inconsistent with the entity's trade corridor
call-back verification recorded as completed but to a number supplied in the instruction
post_transaction_signals: entity-initiated recall within hours once the real executive is reached
beneficiary bank confirms same-day onward transfer or withdrawal
correspondent bank freeze request under cross-border fraud protocols
insurance claim under crime/social-engineering cover
attacks.real_world_grounding: BEC is long-established and among the highest-value reported fraud categories by the FBI IC3. The specific escalation — deepfaked video and voice defeating the human call-back control, including publicly reported multi-million-dollar multi-participant video-call incidents — is documented and recent, which is why this scores well above the classic BEC baseline.
attacks.ethical_notes: Frames the attack around the failure of the call-back control and the transfer-level anomalies defenders can monitor, deliberately omitting any pretext content or impersonation methodology.

attacks.name: Marketplace Listing Scam Exploiting Collect-Request Direction Confusion
attacks.attacker_objective: Extract payment from a marketplace counterparty for goods that do not exist, or invert a sale so the seller pays the buyer while believing they are receiving funds.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Listing generation at scale — original-looking photographs, varied item descriptions, and coherent seller personas with plausible histories — defeats the duplicate-image and template-matching heuristics marketplaces rely on to bulk-remove scam inventory. Conversational automation lets one operator hold many simultaneous negotiation threads in the buyer's language and adapt when the counterparty pushes back. Persona and listing sets are regenerated immediately after enforcement, so account-level bans have short half-life.
kill_chain: payment direction confusion or advance-payment demand
victim authorises push or approves collect request
attacks.transaction_signature: Small-to-mid ticket, high-frequency, many-to-one fan-in: dozens of unrelated payers crediting one VPA or account within a short window, with no matching goods-delivery or merchant settlement footprint. The seller-side variant is distinctive: the victim approves a collect/pull request believing it credits them, producing a debit from an account that has just listed an item — a debit whose direction contradicts the customer's stated intent. Amounts frequently cluster around common resale price points (electronics, furniture, two-wheelers) and around token 'booking advances'.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Beneficiary account is young, has near-zero outbound diversity, and shows fan-in from geographically dispersed, mutually unconnected payers. Payer side shows a first-ever payee, a preceding marketplace app session, and often a chat handoff to an external messaging app. Repeat victims sometimes make a second payment after a fabricated 'transaction failed' claim.
observable_signals: many-to-one credit fan-in to a payee under 60 days old
collect/pull request approved by a customer who is the stated seller
payment to a first-ever payee within minutes of a marketplace app session
duplicate near-identical amounts from unconnected payers same day
second payment to same payee after a claimed failure of the first
military/relocation/urgent-transfer style listing metadata correlated with the payee
post_transaction_signals: clustered complaints naming one VPA or account handle
beneficiary account restricted for mule indicators after fan-in threshold
marketplace trust-and-safety takedown correlating to the same payee
non-delivery disputes filed 3-10 days post-payment
attacks.real_world_grounding: Classified-listing fraud and UPI collect-request direction confusion are both heavily documented in India, prompting NPCI and bank-level restrictions on collect requests from unverified entities. Generative listing and persona content is a documented scaling factor for marketplace abuse rather than a new mechanism.
attacks.ethical_notes: Covers the fan-in and payment-direction anomalies that detection systems key on; it does not explain how to construct listings, personas, or requests.

attacks.name: Cloned-Relative Emergency Payment Under Manufactured Duress
attacks.attacker_objective: Extract an immediate emotionally-coerced transfer by impersonating a family member in crisis, or an authority figure detaining them.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Short samples of a relative's voice, widely available from social video, are sufficient for a distressed-sounding clone — and distress conveniently masks the residual artefacts that would otherwise expose synthesis. Real-time conversion allows the 'relative' to respond briefly before being handed to an authority persona, which is what converts a suspicious call into a compelling one. In the Indian 'digital arrest' variant, video synthesis and generated official-looking documents extend the coercion across many hours, keeping the victim isolated from anyone who could break the spell.
kill_chain: relationship and voice-sample harvesting from open sources
crisis call with cloned relative voice
handoff to authority or medical persona
attacks.transaction_signature: Urgent, often round-number transfers to a first-time payee, sometimes framed as bail, hospital admission, or a compliance deposit. Frequently multiple tranches over hours as the demand escalates. In the digital-arrest variant, transfers may go to accounts styled to look institutional. Genuine device, genuine credentials, no velocity anomaly beyond the payee being new — the authorization stream is essentially clean, which is the core defensive problem.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Atypical hour-of-day for the customer. Session opens with balance checks and limit inquiries. Elderly or low-digital-tenure customers over-represented. Customer is on a continuous call for hours and unreachable by the bank on the same number. Multi-hour, multi-tranche pattern in the coerced-detention variant with the customer refusing to disengage when contacted.
observable_signals: first-ever payee funded within minutes of session start at an atypical hour
customer unreachable on registered mobile during the transaction window
repeated tranches to the same new payee over a multi-hour window
high-value payment from a customer whose historical maximum is far lower
beneficiary account receiving fan-in from multiple elderly-profile payers
warning interstitials dismissed without the usual reading dwell time
post_transaction_signals: family-reported fraud claim, often 12-48 hours late due to shame or isolation
beneficiary drained within minutes of credit
cyber-crime helpline complaint under coercive-detention typology
mule account correlation across several unrelated elderly victims
attacks.real_world_grounding: Voice-cloned relative-in-distress calls and the India-specific 'digital arrest' coercion pattern are both documented by law enforcement, with RBI and Indian police issuing public advisories on the latter. Cheap high-quality voice cloning is what converted a formerly niche scam into a volume one.
attacks.ethical_notes: Restricted to victim-cohort, session-timing, and beneficiary-drain signals used for detection and intervention; contains no cloning method, script, or coercion technique.

attacks.name: Fake Refund And Deliberate Overpayment Reversal Scam
attacks.attacker_objective: Convince the victim that they have been mistakenly overpaid or over-refunded, so they voluntarily 'return' funds that were never genuinely credited or that were credited from another victim.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Generative tooling supplies the two credibility props this scam depends on: convincing refund and credit-confirmation artefacts (transaction advices, support-portal views, SMS-styled confirmations) and a support persona fluent enough to sustain a long walkthrough call. Because the persuasion rests on the victim mis-reading a balance or a document, high-fidelity synthetic artefacts materially raise conversion. Multilingual support personas extend the same operation across regional customer bases at negligible marginal cost.
kill_chain: support-desk pretext over a claimed refund or subscription
layering, sometimes chaining a second victim
attacks.transaction_signature: The strongest tell is a debit that references or approximately matches a recent inbound credit, but goes to a payee unrelated to the original crediting party. Amounts are often odd rather than round (mirroring a fabricated 'excess'). In the chained variant, the inbound credit is real money stolen from a second victim, so the receiving account shows an unusual inbound from an unrelated third party followed by a near-equal outbound — a classic unwitting-mule shape. Card variant appears as a CNP payment to a merchant descriptor unrelated to the original purchase.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Session frequently coincides with a remote-support connection or an inbound call. Customer navigates to transaction history immediately before initiating the outbound. New payee created with a name loosely resembling a known merchant or a payments brand. Customer may repeat the pattern if told the first return 'failed'.
observable_signals: outbound near-equal to a recent unrelated inbound credit
remote-access or screen-share process active during a banking session
inbound credit from a third party with no prior relationship to either side
new payee name approximating a merchant or payment-brand string
transaction-history view immediately preceding a new-payee transfer
repeat transfer after a claimed failure of the first
post_transaction_signals: the crediting party (second victim) raises their own APP claim, exposing the chain
recall request arriving at the intermediate victim's bank
intermediate account restricted pending mule investigation
card dispute filed against an unrelated merchant descriptor
attacks.real_world_grounding: Refund and overpayment scams, including the remote-support-assisted variant and the chained pattern that turns the first victim into an unwitting mule, are long-documented in UK, US, and Indian consumer fraud reporting. GenAI improves the fake-artefact quality and multilingual reach rather than changing the mechanism.
attacks.ethical_notes: Documents the inbound-credit-to-outbound-debit correlation defenders use to unwind chained victim scams, and deliberately excludes any artefact-forgery or pretext detail.

attacks.name: Task-Based Job Scam Escalating Into Unwitting Mule Recruitment
attacks.attacker_objective: Extract escalating 'deposits' from a job seeker while simultaneously converting their bank account into a laundering hop for other victims' funds.
attacks.genai_mechanism: The scam requires a high-touch, many-hours relationship per victim — onboarding chat, task coaching, encouragement after each deposit — which used to cap operator throughput. Conversational automation runs hundreds of these relationships concurrently in local languages, with generated recruiter identities, offer documents, and portal dashboards showing individualised fake earnings. Agentic orchestration can time the escalation prompts to each victim's payment behaviour, which is what makes the deposit ladder tractable at scale.
kill_chain: mass recruitment outreach with generated employer identity
task deposits required to 'unlock' higher tiers
account repurposed as a pass-through hop
victim exposed to mule enforcement while still believing they are employed
attacks.transaction_signature: Two superimposed patterns in the same account, which is the diagnostic feature. Outbound: an escalating deposit ladder to a rotating set of young payees, small early credits back to the victim, then increasingly large one-way payments. Inbound: unrelated third-party credits followed within minutes by near-equal outbound transfers to further new payees — pass-through with negligible residual and no economic rationale. Card rail appears where deposits are funded by CNP wallet top-ups or credit-line drawdowns.
attacks.behavioral_signature: New payee creation rate far above the customer's baseline, sustained over weeks. Account turnover rises by orders of magnitude with no change in declared income or salary credit. Frequently a young or low-tenure customer. Victim defends the activity as employment when questioned and may hold multiple accounts across banks showing the same shape.
observable_signals: escalating one-way deposit ladder to rotating young beneficiaries
inbound third-party credit and near-equal outbound within minutes, repeatedly
monthly turnover far exceeding declared income with near-zero retained balance
new-payee creation rate well above the customer's historical baseline
credit-line drawdown or wallet top-up funding outbound deposits
customer asserts employment relationship when contacted about the flows
post_transaction_signals: victim's account named in another victim's APP recall request
mule-account restriction or lien applied by the bank or on police reference
victim files their own fraud claim only after withdrawal is refused
cross-institution correlation showing the same customer as a hop in several fraud chains
attacks.real_world_grounding: Task and part-time-job scams are among the fastest-growing reported frauds in India and Southeast Asia, and the dual role of the victim as both payer and money-mule is documented in bank mule-account enforcement and police advisories. Conversational automation is a credible and partly-observed scaling factor for the high-touch relationship the scam requires.
attacks.ethical_notes: Describes the account-turnover and pass-through signatures that let institutions identify and protect unwitting mules, without any recruitment, laundering, or persona-construction detail.

attacks.name: Synthetic Merchant Onboarding With Generated Business Document Packages
attacks.attacker_objective: Obtain a live merchant ID and settlement account under a shell or non-existent business so that fraud proceeds can be acquired and settled through legitimate payment infrastructure.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Generative models let an applicant produce an internally consistent corporate identity package at near-zero marginal cost: a plausible trade name and business narrative, a coherent website with product catalogue and policy pages, matching invoices and statement layouts, and synthetic director portrait imagery that survives casual visual review. The consistency is the differentiator — pre-GenAI shell applications tended to fail cross-field coherence checks (address vs tax registration vs website vs bank narration), whereas generated packages align these fields, so underwriting must rely on independent external verification rather than internal plausibility. Model-assisted variation also makes each application in a batch look unrelated, weakening duplicate-text and template-reuse detection at the acquirer.
attacks.transaction_signature: After activation, a near-vertical volume curve from zero to policy limits within days; ticket sizes clustered tightly just under the acquirer's manual-review threshold; the MCC assigned at onboarding (often low-risk retail or professional services) is inconsistent with the actual basket mix; cardholder BIN geography broadly dispersed with no local catchment consistent with the claimed physical address.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Merchant portal is accessed from a small set of devices and IP ranges shared with other recently onboarded merchant accounts; no customer-service traffic, no partial refunds, no seasonality; the settlement bank account is newly opened and immediately swept in full after each payout cycle; the claimed storefront shows no organic traffic history or crawl age matching the stated incorporation date.
observable_signals: Merchant age under 90 days with volume ramp exceeding underwriting projection by a large multiple
Device, browser fingerprint, or portal login IP shared across multiple distinct legal entities
Settlement bank account opened within days of the merchant application
Website domain registration age inconsistent with claimed business tenure; thin or templated policy pages
Director identity documents that pass format checks but fail independent registry or liveness cross-verification
Full sweep of settlement credits to third-party accounts within hours of payout
post_transaction_signals: Chargeback ratio crossing network monitoring thresholds within the first two to three settlement cycles
Acquirer unable to contact the merchant for retrieval requests or compelling-evidence responses
Settlement account frozen or reported by the sponsor bank as a mule after payout
Cardholder disputes citing an unrecognised descriptor that maps to the shell trade name
attacks.real_world_grounding: Fraudulent merchant onboarding is a long-standing acquiring risk addressed by card-network integrity programs and, in India, by RBI payment-aggregator due-diligence obligations for sub-merchant onboarding. The generative element is a documented and rapidly growing extension: synthetic document and identity packages have been reported by KYC vendors at materially rising rates since 2023.
attacks.ethical_notes: The entry describes underwriting and settlement-side consequences an acquirer can measure; it contains no document-forgery method, verification-bypass technique, or onboarding script.

attacks.name: Collusive Merchant Settlement Bust-Out With Fraudster-Supplied Card Data
attacks.attacker_objective: Convert stolen or compromised card credentials into bank-settled funds by running them through a real, established merchant whose operator knowingly participates and shares the proceeds.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Unlike a shell merchant, the entity here is genuine and has trading history, so the attacker's problem is pacing rather than plausibility. Language models are used to reason over the merchant's own historical volume, ticket distribution, and refund patterns and to propose an injection schedule that stays inside the merchant's normal statistical envelope until the final extraction window. The same capability drafts the merchant's dispute responses and acquirer correspondence in a register consistent with the business's prior communications, delaying the point at which the acquirer escalates.
kill_chain: Merchant recruitment or takeover of an existing MID
attacks.transaction_signature: Authorizations that individually match the merchant's established MCC, currency, and ticket-size profile, so per-transaction scoring is weak; the anomaly is compositional — a step change in the ratio of new-to-repeat cardholders, a rise in the share of BINs outside the merchant's historical issuing footprint, and card-present terminals presenting keyed or fallback entry modes inconsistent with the terminal's prior EMV behaviour.
attacks.behavioral_signature: The merchant's operational telemetry decouples from its payment telemetry: order volume rises while inventory movement, shipping labels, support tickets, and web sessions do not. Refund rate collapses toward zero even as volume rises. The merchant begins requesting faster settlement, higher limits, or reserve release shortly before the volume spike.
observable_signals: Step change in share of first-time cardholders at an established merchant
Issuing-BIN geography broadening abruptly against the merchant's own baseline
Refund and partial-refund rate falling to near zero during a volume increase
Card-present entry-mode drift toward keyed or magstripe fallback on EMV-capable terminals
Merchant-initiated requests for reserve release, limit increase, or settlement acceleration preceding the spike
Divergence between payment volume and non-payment operational signals such as logistics or session counts
post_transaction_signals: Chargeback cluster arriving 30 to 90 days later, concentrated in fraud reason codes rather than service reason codes
Merchant becomes unresponsive or ceases trading once the reserve is exhausted
Acquirer loss materialising because settled funds were withdrawn before disputes landed
Overlap of disputed card numbers with credentials seen at other collusive MIDs in the same acquirer portfolio
attacks.real_world_grounding: Collusive and bust-out merchants are among the oldest documented acquiring-side losses and are the reason acquirers hold rolling reserves and run chargeback-monitoring programs. GenAI changes the pacing and correspondence quality, not the fundamental pattern.
attacks.ethical_notes: It characterises portfolio-level and settlement-timing consequences visible to an acquirer, with no guidance on recruiting merchants, sourcing credentials, or evading reserves.

attacks.name: Transaction Laundering Through A Legitimate-Looking Front Merchant
attacks.attacker_objective: Process payments for an undisclosed, prohibited, or unlicensed business by routing them through the merchant identity and MCC of an approved, benign-looking storefront.
attacks.genai_mechanism: The economics of laundering depend on maintaining a convincing cover storefront that no one actually buys from, and generative tooling makes that cover cheap and continuously refreshable: catalogue copy, product imagery, reviews, blog content, and localisation for whatever MCC the front claims. When a cover site is flagged, an equivalent replacement with different text, imagery, and layout can be stood up quickly, which weakens the content-similarity and template-matching heuristics that transaction-laundering scanners have relied on. The generative layer raises the cost of content-based detection and pushes defenders toward payment-flow and network evidence.
kill_chain: Undisclosed traffic routed to the approved MID
attacks.transaction_signature: Authorization mix that does not fit the registered MCC — for example a claimed home-goods or education merchant showing round-number ticket amounts, high repeat-payer frequency, unusual hour-of-day concentration, and cross-border cardholder distribution characteristic of a different vertical. The descriptor shown to cardholders matches the benign front while refund and decline behaviour matches the hidden business. On UPI and A2A, the equivalent signature is a P2M VPA whose inbound payer set and amount distribution do not match the registered merchant category.
attacks.behavioral_signature: The advertised storefront receives almost no organic browsing sessions relative to its transaction count — checkout events vastly outnumber product-page views, and payment initiations arrive with referrers or deep links from outside the site. The same settlement account, beneficial owner, device fingerprints, or support contact details recur across several unrelated front merchants.
observable_signals: Checkout-to-browse ratio implausibly high for the claimed retail vertical
Basket and ticket distribution inconsistent with the registered MCC
Payment initiations arriving without a session on the merchant's own storefront
Shared settlement account, beneficial owner, or contact detail across multiple unrelated MIDs
Cardholder or payer geography with no relationship to the front's stated market
Rapid replacement of a flagged storefront by a near-equivalent new domain under the same payment relationship
post_transaction_signals: Disputes whose cardholder description of the purchase does not match the merchant's stated product line
Network integrity-program notification or fine to the acquirer for undisclosed aggregation
Regulatory or law-enforcement referral tying the settlement flow to an unlicensed activity
Chargebacks concentrated in service and misrepresentation reason codes rather than counterfeit
attacks.real_world_grounding: Transaction laundering is explicitly targeted by card-network integrity and brand-protection programs and by payment-aggregator obligations to know their sub-merchants; content-generation tooling is a documented accelerant for disposable cover storefronts.
attacks.ethical_notes: The entry stays at the level of flow-level mismatches an acquirer or scheme can measure and deliberately omits how cover infrastructure is built or rotated.

attacks.name: Industrialised Refund And Item-Not-Received Abuse Against Merchant Support
attacks.attacker_objective: Extract cash refunds or replacement goods from merchants at scale by asserting non-delivery, damage, or empty-box claims on transactions that were genuinely authorised and genuinely delivered.
attacks.genai_mechanism: The bottleneck in refund abuse has always been human effort per claim — a persuasive, non-repetitive complaint written in the right register for each merchant's support policy. Language models remove that bottleneck, producing individually varied claim narratives, escalation follow-ups, and policy-citing rebuttals across hundreds of orders, and image models can supply damage or wrong-item photographs consistent with the claimed SKU. Because each claim reads as unique and emotionally plausible, merchant support teams and text-similarity heuristics lose the duplicate-language signal they previously relied on.
attacks.transaction_signature: The authorizations themselves are clean and fully compliant — correct cardholder, passing 3DS or UPI PIN, normal amounts and MCCs — so there is effectively no distinctive authorization footprint. The signature appears only in the refund and credit stream: a rising ratio of full-value credits to sales for particular customer cohorts, and refunds issued without a corresponding return receipt or reverse-logistics scan.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Account cohorts with normal purchase behaviour but abnormal post-purchase behaviour: high claim rate concentrated in high-resale-value SKUs, claims filed within a narrow window after delivery confirmation, delivery addresses that recur across nominally different accounts, and refund destinations that drift away from the original payment instrument toward wallets or bank accounts.
observable_signals: Claim rate per account far exceeding cohort baseline, concentrated in resaleable categories
Refund requested to an instrument or account different from the original payment source
Delivery address, phone, or device shared across multiple claiming accounts
Refund issued with no reverse-logistics pickup or warehouse receipt event
Claim narratives that are linguistically varied but structurally identical in claim type and timing
Repeat claims following a fixed lag after carrier delivery confirmation
post_transaction_signals: Merchant refund-to-sales ratio breaching internal thresholds for a specific customer cohort
Escalation to issuer chargeback when the merchant declines the refund
Refunded goods reappearing in secondary marketplace listings
Cluster linkage revealing one address or device behind many refunded orders
attacks.real_world_grounding: Refund abuse operated as a paid service against large e-commerce merchants is a well documented and prosecuted pattern, and merchants publicly report post-purchase abuse now rivalling stolen-card losses in some categories. Generative content is a credible and already-observed force multiplier on claim volume.
attacks.ethical_notes: It describes refund-stream and logistics-side consequences merchants already measure, without any claim template, evidence-fabrication method, or targeting guidance.

attacks.name: First-Party Misuse With AI-Drafted Dispute Narratives
attacks.attacker_objective: Reverse a legitimate, cardholder-authorised purchase by constructing a dispute narrative that maps cleanly onto a favourable reason code and survives merchant representment.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Dispute outcomes hinge on how a customer's account of events is framed against reason-code definitions and evidence requirements, which is exactly the kind of structured rewriting language models do well. A disputant can have their sequence of events restated in the vocabulary of unauthorised use, non-receipt, or cancelled recurring service, with internally consistent dates and a coherent second round of rebuttal when the merchant submits compelling evidence. This is distinct from refund abuse because the counterparty is the issuer and the scheme dispute process rather than merchant support, and the mechanism scales narrative quality rather than claim volume.
attacks.transaction_signature: No distinctive authorization footprint at all — the transaction is genuine, device- and geolocation-consistent with the cardholder, and typically strongly authenticated via 3DS or UPI PIN. The abuse is invisible in the authorization stream by construction; only the later dispute record distinguishes it.
attacks.behavioral_signature: The disputing account continues to use the same device and instrument at the same merchant, or at close substitutes, after filing an unauthorised-use claim. Dispute filings cluster after digital goods are fully consumed, after subscription value is extracted, or shortly after a billing cycle. Narrative sophistication of the claim is out of step with the account holder's own historical support interactions.
observable_signals: Dispute filed on a transaction that passed strong customer authentication on a long-tenured device
Continued account activity at the disputed merchant after an unauthorised-use claim
Disputes concentrated on digital, downloadable, or fully-consumed services
Rising per-account dispute count across unrelated merchants within an issuing portfolio
Dispute wording tightly mirroring reason-code evidentiary language
Filing timed just inside the scheme or regulatory dispute window
post_transaction_signals: Issuer chargeback under a fraud reason code on a strongly authenticated transaction
Merchant representment overturned despite delivery and authentication evidence
Repeat disputant identified only via cross-merchant or scheme-level negative-list matching
Provisional credit never recovered after the dispute cycle closes
attacks.real_world_grounding: First-party misuse is the fastest-growing dispute category reported by issuers and merchants, and the card schemes have introduced dedicated first-party-misuse handling and pre-dispute data sharing in response. AI-assisted narrative drafting is a credible near-term amplifier already visible in consumer-facing dispute tooling.
attacks.ethical_notes: The entry documents why authentication evidence alone does not stop these disputes and what defenders can correlate afterward; it supplies no reason-code playbook or dispute wording.

attacks.name: Mule-Network Fan-In And Layering Across A2A And UPI Rails
attacks.attacker_objective: Move scam and fraud proceeds through a disposable network of third-party accounts fast enough to break traceability before recall or freeze orders can catch up.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Mule networks are constrained by recruitment throughput and by coordination across many low-trust participants. Language models scale the recruitment side by producing persuasive, localised part-time-income messaging in multiple Indian languages at conversational volume, and agentic orchestration coordinates hop timing and value splitting across the collection layer so no single account presents an obviously abnormal profile. The defensive consequence is that per-account thresholds degrade further and detection must move to graph structure.
kill_chain: Victim funds collected into first-layer accounts
Rapid multi-hop layering and value splitting
Cash-out at terminal accounts or via goods
attacks.transaction_signature: Individually unremarkable credits and debits, mostly below reporting and review thresholds. The pattern exists only in aggregate: high payee fan-in where many unrelated remitters credit one account within a short window, followed by fan-out to a fresh set of beneficiaries, with per-hop dwell time of minutes; near-total pass-through ratio; round or near-round amounts just under structuring thresholds; and a burst-then-dormancy lifecycle per account.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Accounts are recently opened, or long dormant then suddenly reactivated. Device and SIM binding is shared across many accounts, or one device successively binds many VPAs. Balances never accumulate — funds are transient. Beneficiary lists are large and non-recurring. Login and transaction hours cluster tightly across the cohort, indicating shared operation rather than independent account holders.
observable_signals: Payee fan-in from many unrelated remitters within a short window
Pass-through ratio approaching one with minutes-scale dwell time
One device or SIM associated with many distinct accounts or VPAs
Dormant account reactivating with immediate high-velocity transfer activity
Beneficiary sets that are large, one-time, and non-overlapping with history
Amounts consistently just below internal review or reporting thresholds
post_transaction_signals: Inbound recall or freeze requests from multiple originating banks converging on the same account
Victim complaints filed through national cybercrime reporting arriving after funds have already hopped out
Terminal-layer cash withdrawal or voucher conversion at the network edge
Graph analysis linking seemingly independent accounts through shared devices or beneficiaries
attacks.real_world_grounding: Mule-account layering on instant rails is a documented and heavily prosecuted problem in India, and the RBI Innovation Hub's MuleHunter initiative exists specifically because single-account rules fail against these graph patterns. AI-assisted multilingual recruitment is an observed accelerant.
attacks.ethical_notes: The entry describes graph-level indicators and recall dynamics that banks and regulators already act on, and deliberately omits recruitment content, hop timing, or threshold values.

attacks.name: Gift-Card And Voucher Conversion As A Terminal Cash-Out Layer
attacks.attacker_objective: Convert fraudulently obtained card, wallet, or account balances into bearer-style stored value that can be resold for clean funds outside the payment network's reach.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Voucher conversion is attractive because value becomes a bearer instrument the instant a code is issued, and its constraint is purchase throughput across many merchant and aggregator surfaces before the source funds are frozen. Agents capable of operating ordinary consumer checkout flows compress that window substantially, and generative content supports the resale side with convincing listings and buyer-facing support messaging on secondary marketplaces. Defensively this means the recoverable window shrinks from hours to minutes.
kill_chain: Source funds obtained via card, scam, or account takeover
attacks.transaction_signature: Concentrated authorizations at gift-card, voucher-aggregator, prepaid top-up, and digital-goods MCCs; multiple purchases in rapid succession at or just under per-transaction voucher caps; many distinct cards or VPAs converging on a small set of voucher merchants; delivery to disposable email addresses; frequent same-instrument retries after declines to maximise conversion before the instrument is blocked.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Purchasing accounts have no consumption history in the voucher category, no prior relationship with the brands purchased, and no gifting pattern such as recipient names or scheduled delivery. Redemption occurs from geographies and devices unrelated to the purchaser within minutes. In the scam-driven variant the victim themselves performs the purchase under coercion, so the buyer profile is entirely genuine and only the redemption side is anomalous.
observable_signals: Burst of voucher or prepaid MCC authorizations from an account with no such history
Many distinct funding instruments converging on one voucher merchant in a short window
Voucher delivery to disposable or newly created email addresses
Redemption device and geography disjoint from purchase device and geography
Purchase amounts pinned to per-transaction voucher caps
Repeated retries immediately following declines on the same instrument
post_transaction_signals: Chargebacks on the funding cards after codes are already redeemed and unrecoverable
Victim scam reports describing coerced voucher purchase, filed after redemption
Voucher codes surfacing on secondary resale markets at a discount to face value
Issuer recovery attempts failing because the voucher issuer treats the code as bearer value
attacks.real_world_grounding: Gift-card cash-out is a documented terminal stage in both stolen-credential fraud and coercive scam typologies, and consumer-protection agencies publish standing warnings about voucher-based scam payments. Agentic checkout automation is a credible near-term compression of the recovery window.
attacks.ethical_notes: It describes conversion-stage signals and the recovery gap defenders face; it names no merchants, caps, or automation methods that would assist a cash-out.

attacks.name: Fake Marketplace Sellers And Triangulation Fraud
attacks.attacker_objective: Collect clean payments from genuine buyers on a marketplace while fulfilling their orders using stolen card credentials at unrelated retailers, so the fraud loss lands on third parties.
attacks.genai_mechanism: A triangulation seller must look like a real store to buyers and to marketplace trust teams, which historically required scraped or stolen listing content that duplicate-detection could find. Generative models produce original product descriptions, category-appropriate imagery, storefront branding, and buyer-support messaging per seller account, so a fresh seller identity can present as an established small business and rotate cheaply after suspension. This shifts marketplace defence away from content matching and toward fulfilment-side and network-linkage evidence.
kill_chain: Seller account creation with generated storefront identity
Below-market listing and genuine buyer acquisition
Fulfilment via compromised credentials at third-party retailers
attacks.transaction_signature: Two separate and superficially healthy authorization streams that only reveal the fraud when joined. On the marketplace side, buyer payments are fully legitimate and dispute-free. On the retailer side, card-not-present authorizations show a persistent mismatch between billing identity and shipping recipient, one payment instrument shipping to many unrelated addresses, and order composition matching another marketplace's live listings.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Seller accounts are young, priced consistently below market, and carry no return or reverse-logistics history because the seller holds no inventory. Buyer satisfaction is initially high, which suppresses marketplace risk scores. Seller payout accounts, devices, or contact details recur across suspended predecessors. On the retailer side, guest checkouts from fresh accounts repeatedly ship to third-party names.
observable_signals: New seller with below-market pricing and no inventory or reverse-logistics footprint
Retailer orders where billing and shipping identities never match, repeatedly, on one instrument
Single payment instrument shipping to many unrelated recipient names and addresses
Payout bank account or device shared with previously suspended seller identities
Marketplace listing content mirroring another retailer's live catalogue in SKU and availability
Buyer complaints of receiving goods in third-party retailer packaging
post_transaction_signals: Chargebacks landing at the fulfilling retailer weeks later, with recipients who deny ordering
Marketplace payout already withdrawn before the retailer disputes mature
Cardholder disputes naming a retailer the cardholder never visited
Cross-platform linkage showing one operator behind several suspended seller identities
attacks.real_world_grounding: Triangulation fraud is a well documented marketplace typology with prosecutions and public retailer advisories; generated storefront content is an already-visible extension that undermines duplicate-listing detection.
attacks.ethical_notes: The entry explains why the loss is displaced onto retailers and which cross-party linkages expose it, without describing seller-onboarding evasion or fulfilment methods.

attacks.name: QR Substitution And Payment-Link Redirection At Merchant Points Of Acceptance
attacks.attacker_objective: Divert payments intended for a genuine merchant into an attacker-controlled payee by substituting the acceptance artefact — a static QR at the till or a shared payment link — rather than by compromising any credential.
attacks.genai_mechanism: This attack depends entirely on the payment artefact looking authentic in the two seconds a payer inspects it, and generative tooling makes brand-accurate replicas of merchant standees, in-app confirmation screens, invoices, and payment-request messages easy to produce in the right regional language and branding. Voice and messaging models additionally sustain a live conversation asserting that a payment failed and must be retried against a different payee, or that a refund requires an approval action. The consequence for defenders is that payer-side visual and conversational verification becomes unreliable, and trust must move to the payee-identity data the app itself renders.
kill_chain: Acceptance artefact substituted or spoofed link distributed
Payer initiates a fully authenticated payment to the wrong payee
Immediate onward layering from the receiving account
Merchant discovers the shortfall at reconciliation
attacks.transaction_signature: Authorization-side appearance is entirely normal — a genuine payer, a genuine device, correct PIN or authentication, and an ordinary amount. The only payment-stream anomaly is on the receiving side: a payee accumulating many small payments from payers physically clustered around a merchant location it has no registered relationship with, and a merchant whose settled volume drops without a corresponding drop in footfall or till activity. Collect-request variants show an inbound debit-request pattern where a merchant-initiated push would be expected.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Payer sessions show a scan or link-open immediately followed by payment with no prior relationship to the payee VPA or account. Receiving accounts are newly created, briefly very active within one geographic cell, then dormant. In the coached refund or failed-payment variant, the payer's session shows an unusually long pre-payment dwell consistent with being talked through the flow, and sometimes a screen-sharing or remote-assistance application running concurrently.
observable_signals: Payee VPA or account receiving many small payments from payers concentrated at one merchant location without a registered merchant link
Merchant settled volume diverging from till, footfall, or invoice counts
Payment initiated seconds after a scan or link-open to a first-time payee
Remote-access or screen-sharing application active on the payer device during initiation
Inbound collect-request pattern where the merchant relationship implies a push payment
Receiving account newly opened, geographically narrow, and dormant shortly after a burst
post_transaction_signals: Merchant reconciliation shortfall reported days later against physical sales records
Victim complaints filed through cybercrime channels naming an unrecognised payee
Funds already layered out of the receiving account before any freeze request lands
Clustered complaints from multiple payers naming the same beneficiary account
attacks.real_world_grounding: QR-substitution and collect-request misuse are documented and widely warned-about fraud patterns on Indian instant-payment rails, and remote-assistance-assisted payment diversion is a recurring complaint category. Multimodal brand-accurate spoofing is a realistic and partly observed amplifier.
attacks.ethical_notes: The entry is written from the payee-side and reconciliation-side view a bank or merchant can act on, and contains no artefact-substitution technique, link construction, or social-engineering script.

attacks.name: Decline-Code Oracle Threshold Mapping
attacks.attacker_objective: Recover an approximate map of the issuer's and acquirer's risk thresholds so that later high-value fraud can be placed inside the approve region on the first attempt.
attacks.genai_mechanism: The approve / decline / soft-decline response is a free label, and LLM-driven agents turn a probing campaign into an adaptive experiment-design loop: they summarise thousands of noisy responses into a compact surrogate of where the boundary sits and propose which attribute region to sample next. What previously required a skilled analyst reading spreadsheets of response codes now runs continuously and cheaply. The generative contribution is hypothesis generation and result compression, not any new payment capability.
kill_chain: targeted cash-out inside the approve region
attacks.transaction_signature: Dense clusters of very low value or zero-value account-verification authorisations spread across many BINs but concentrated on a handful of merchant IDs; near-lattice amount ladders that step in regular increments; abnormally high ratio of soft declines and step-up requests to approvals; approvals frequently abandoned rather than captured.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Enormous fan-out across PANs and VPAs with almost no repeat use per instrument; checkout sessions with no browsing, cart, or product-page dwell; inter-attempt spacing locked tightly to the previous response latency rather than to any human rhythm; probing pauses and resumes in lockstep with rule changes on the defender side.
observable_signals: approval rate per merchant per BIN collapsing below a historical floor
elevated share of zero-value or nominal-value verification authorisations
low entropy and regular-increment structure in attempted amounts
inter-attempt interval correlated with authorisation response time
approved authorisations that are never captured or settled
single merchant descriptor receiving traffic from implausibly many issuers
post_transaction_signals: near-zero chargeback rate on the probe traffic itself, followed by a concentrated fraud burst on the mapped segment
scheme excessive-authorisation-attempt monitoring flags at the acquirer
merchant-level authorisation-to-capture ratio breaching normal range
attacks.real_world_grounding: Card-testing and BIN-attack traffic against small merchants and donation pages is a long-documented pattern, and issuers already monitor authorisation-attempt ratios for it; the newer element is systematic reuse of the responses as training labels for a surrogate model rather than as a simple validity check.
attacks.ethical_notes: The entry describes the aggregate authorisation-stream footprint a defender can measure and the monitoring metrics that surface it, with no probing methodology, tooling, or response-code exploitation detail.

attacks.name: Victim Ticket-Distribution Amount Mimicry
attacks.attacker_objective: Extract value from a compromised instrument using charge amounts drawn from the victim's own historical spend distribution so amount-deviation features never fire.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Where the attacker already holds statement data, an account-aggregator view, or scraped transaction SMS, a language model can compress that history into a spend profile and a sequence model can sample amounts conditioned on merchant type, so each individual charge sits near the victim's modal ticket rather than at a round attacker-convenient figure. The capability that matters is cheap per-victim personalisation at population scale — previously fraud rings used one amount policy for every stolen card.
kill_chain: extraction ahead of the statement cycle
attacks.transaction_signature: Charges clustered around the victim's personal modal ticket rather than at classic test-and-escalate values; no single outlier amount; total daily spend inflated well above baseline while every constituent amount is unremarkable; amounts often lacking the natural catalogue-price structure of genuine retail spend.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Spend level and rhythm look familiar while the merchant set is almost entirely new to the account; the amount distribution is unnaturally tight around the mode with the long right tail of real consumer spending missing; no returns, no partial reversals, no abandoned carts.
observable_signals: cumulative daily or rolling-window spend far above baseline despite in-range per-transaction amounts
amount variance below the victim's own historical variance
absence of the long-tail high-ticket component present in genuine history
merchant novelty rate near one hundred percent within the burst
amount values not matching known catalogue price points for the claimed merchant
basket composition inconsistent with the amount for that merchant category
post_transaction_signals: clustered cardholder disputes filed after the statement or SMS review
chargebacks concentrated on merchants the account never used before
refund requests never initiated by the genuine cardholder for the disputed items
attacks.real_world_grounding: Amount-tuning to avoid velocity and deviation rules is established fraud tradecraft; what generative tooling changes is the economics of doing it per victim rather than per campaign, which is a credible near-term extrapolation from observed data-broker and aggregator leakage in India.
attacks.ethical_notes: It states which detector feature is neutralised and which aggregate and structural residuals survive, without describing how to obtain victim history or construct amount schedules.

attacks.name: Diurnal Rhythm Timing Mimicry
attacks.attacker_objective: Place fraudulent activity inside the victim's habitual transacting hours so that odd-hour rules and time-of-day risk features contribute nothing to the score.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Agentic orchestration lets a single operator run thousands of compromised accounts on individually inferred schedules rather than firing everything during the operator's own working hours. A model infers each account's active window from observed history and drives execution into it, and can also introduce plausible jitter so the sequence does not look machine-scheduled. The novelty is per-account scheduling at scale, not the idea of transacting during the day.
attacks.transaction_signature: No odd-hour footprint at all; authorisations land inside the account's usual active band and on the usual weekday pattern, and the burst is disguised as an ordinary busy day. The distinctive footprint is compression rather than displacement — a normal day's worth of activity delivered in an atypically dense run inside the normal window.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Inter-arrival gaps are too regular and under-dispersed compared with genuine human spacing; session start times cluster to the minute across unrelated accounts run by the same operator; device idle and dwell patterns do not show the interruptions of real use; occasionally the victim is genuinely active elsewhere at the same moment.
observable_signals: inter-transaction gap distribution under-dispersed relative to the account's own history
identical minute-of-hour start alignment across unrelated accounts
in-window transaction density far above the account's historical maximum
session interaction dwell time near-constant across steps
concurrent genuine victim session from a different device or geography
device local clock or app timezone inconsistent with the claimed active window
post_transaction_signals: victim disputes describing normal-hours transactions they did not make
mule beneficiary receiving inbound credits from many accounts within the same narrow daily band
recall requests concentrated on a single operator-aligned time slot
attacks.real_world_grounding: Time-of-day features and night-time step-up rules are standard in issuer models, and fraud operations shifting into victim-normal hours has been observed for years; generative orchestration mainly raises the number of accounts one operator can schedule individually.
attacks.ethical_notes: The description stays at the level of arrival-time statistics a defender can compute, and names no scheduling technique or evasion procedure.

attacks.name: Sub-Threshold Velocity Shaping Across Rails And Instruments
attacks.attacker_objective: Move the full value of a compromised position while keeping every per-instrument, per-rail, and per-window counter below the thresholds that would trigger a velocity rule.
attacks.genai_mechanism: An agent can hold the full constraint set — per-transaction ceilings, daily caps, new-payee cooling periods, and separate counters across cards, UPI handles, wallets, and account-to-account rails — and plan an outflow schedule that satisfies all of them at once while maximising throughput. Solving that allocation by hand across dozens of instruments is slow and error-prone; automated planning makes it routine and lets the plan re-solve when a rule changes. The generative contribution is constraint reasoning and replanning, not access to any new rail.
attacks.transaction_signature: Each instrument shows a modest, rule-compliant number of modest transfers; no single counter is anomalous. The pattern is only visible when values are summed across instruments and rails — a large aggregate outflow assembled from many compliant slices, often mixing UPI, immediate account transfers, wallet loads, and card-on-file charges within the same hour.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Nominally independent instruments that share a device, session, or network range; outflows across those instruments tightly coordinated in time; a small set of destination accounts and virtual addresses that many unrelated sources converge on; every window closing just under its limit rather than at a naturally varied level.
observable_signals: outflow counters repeatedly finishing just below their configured limits
many unrelated source accounts converging on a small beneficiary set
shared device or session fingerprint across supposedly independent instruments
aggregate cross-rail outflow far exceeding any single-rail baseline
sudden in-degree spike on beneficiary accounts or virtual payment addresses
total outflow approaching available balance despite unremarkable per-transaction values
post_transaction_signals: beneficiary accounts fanning out or cashing out within minutes of receipt
clustered recall requests naming the same downstream accounts
mule accounts frozen holding balances inconsistent with their declared profile
disputes arriving from many unrelated sources against one destination cluster
attacks.real_world_grounding: Structuring under limits is a long-established laundering and fraud technique, and mule networks converging on shared beneficiary accounts is a well-documented pattern in Indian real-time payments enforcement; automated multi-rail planning is the incremental change.
attacks.ethical_notes: It describes only the aggregate and counterparty-side convergence signals defenders use to detect structuring, and gives no limits, allocation logic, or instrument-mixing guidance.

attacks.name: Geographic Plausibility Manipulation
attacks.attacker_objective: Present a location profile consistent with the victim's home region so that impossible-travel, country-mismatch, and distance-from-home features contribute no risk.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Generative tooling maintains the coherence that used to break location spoofing: a persona whose address, postal code, phone series, language and dialect in support chat, and choice of local merchants all agree with the claimed city. Combined with residential and mobile-carrier exit points inside the victim's own network region, this turns a set of individually checkable location signals into a mutually consistent story. The model contributes the consistency layer, not the network access.
attacks.transaction_signature: Authorisations originate from the victim's city and often the victim's own network operator, address verification matches, and the merchant selection is regionally plausible; there is no cross-border or impossible-travel footprint at all. Delivery, where physical, goes to an address in the same city that the account has never used.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Fine-grained network churn beneath a stable apparent city — the exit point changes far more often than a residential connection does; on app rails the device location and the network-derived location disagree, or location permission is withheld entirely; round-trip latency is inconsistent with the claimed proximity; the same residential exit point reappears across victims with no other relationship.
observable_signals: network exit point churning rapidly within a stable claimed city
device location absent or inconsistent with network-derived location
round-trip latency incompatible with the claimed location
delivery address in-city but never previously used by the account
device locale, keyboard, or SIM region drifting from the claimed home region
one residential exit point shared across otherwise unrelated accounts
post_transaction_signals: chargebacks where address verification passed but the cardholder never received goods
reshipping and drop-address clusters surfacing in dispute investigations
recovered goods traced to addresses linked to multiple unrelated fraud cases
attacks.real_world_grounding: Residential proxy abuse to defeat geolocation controls and local drop addresses to defeat address verification are both well documented in card-not-present fraud; the generative element is cheap maintenance of persona coherence across the address, language, and merchant-choice signals defenders cross-check.
attacks.ethical_notes: The entry enumerates the location residuals that survive spoofing from a defender's telemetry perspective and names no infrastructure, service, or configuration.

attacks.name: Composite In-Range Feature Assembly
attacks.attacker_objective: Keep the model score under the action threshold by holding every individual feature inside the victim's normal range, conceding a little on many axes instead of a lot on one.
attacks.genai_mechanism: This is the category's core problem: a surrogate of the defender's scoring behaviour lets an adversary search for configurations that are simultaneously acceptable on amount, time, merchant, device, and geography while still paying out. Generative search over that feasible region, plus agentic execution across many accounts, converts what was once an artisanal per-target exercise into a repeatable optimisation. No single marginal feature is anomalous, which is exactly what defeats models and rules built on marginal thresholds.
kill_chain: feasible-region search under a score budget
payout within the tolerated risk envelope
attacks.transaction_signature: Authorisations that are individually unremarkable on every axis a rule inspects — in-profile amount, familiar hour, plausible category, recognised device class, home-region origin — yet arrive as a coherent set that no genuine account produces. There is deliberately no single distinctive marker in the authorisation record.
attacks.behavioral_signature: The joint configuration sits off the manifold of real behaviour: a category the victim uses only on weekday mornings appearing at the hour the victim uses only for banking, from the device the victim uses only for something else. Feature-interaction terms and joint-density scores flag what marginal thresholds cannot. Throughput is also visibly constrained — the score budget forces small, slow payouts, so the campaign compensates with breadth across many accounts.
observable_signals: low joint-density score under a learned behavioural model despite all marginals in range
unusual feature-interaction combinations absent from the account's own history
scores clustering just beneath the action threshold rather than spreading naturally
the same near-threshold configuration recurring across unrelated accounts
payout amounts capped in a way that suggests an external constraint rather than opportunity
breadth across accounts substituting for depth within any one account
post_transaction_signals: disputes arriving from many accounts that individually scored as low risk
fraud losses concentrated in a narrow score band just below the threshold
common downstream beneficiaries linking cases that shared no marginal feature
attacks.real_world_grounding: Adversarial evasion of deployed classifiers is well established in the machine-learning literature and increasingly reported in fraud-model operations, where losses concentrating just under an action threshold is a recognised warning sign; the fully automated, per-account form of it is a credible near-term extrapolation.
attacks.ethical_notes: It explains why marginal-threshold defences fail and what joint-distribution and score-band monitoring reveals, without describing surrogate construction, feature manipulation, or any search procedure.

attacks.name: Low-And-Slow Baseline Conditioning
attacks.attacker_objective: Move the account's own behavioural baseline over weeks so that when the payout finally happens it registers as in-profile rather than anomalous.
attacks.genai_mechanism: Personal-baseline features are the defence this attack targets, and they are learned from whatever history the account accumulates. An agent can maintain a long, patient conditioning schedule across a large portfolio of victim and mule accounts — introducing small legitimate-looking activity, seasoning payees, and letting limit increases mature — where a human operator would lose track or lose patience. The generative contribution is durable multi-week campaign management at scale, not any individual transaction.
attacks.transaction_signature: Weeks of small, low-margin, unremarkable activity that establishes tolerance for new categories and counterparties, followed by a payout that no longer looks like a step change against the drifted baseline. The conditioning traffic itself is economically pointless — it exists to move a statistic, not to buy anything.
attacks.behavioral_signature: A baseline that normally stays stationary instead drifts monotonically in one direction; payees are added and then deliberately left unused past any cooling window; the account's behavioural entropy is inconsistent with its apparent tenure; on mule accounts, activity is manufactured rather than organic and lacks the incidental clutter of real life.
observable_signals: monotone drift in a baseline statistic that is normally stationary for that account
payees added and left unused for an extended period before first use
conditioning transactions with no economic rationale or trivially reversible
limit-increase requests preceding a behaviour change rather than following one
account tenure inconsistent with the diversity of its transaction history
step change in outflow that is large against tenure-adjusted history even if small against the drifted baseline
post_transaction_signals: dispute or recall arriving weeks after the conditioning began, when the trail is cold
mule accounts with long quiet histories cashing out in a single episode
forensic review showing the seasoning activity was attacker-controlled or self-refunded
attacks.real_world_grounding: Mule-account ageing and deliberate seasoning ahead of a cash-out is a documented pattern in account-opening and real-time-payment fraud, and account-takeover operations are observed adding payees well ahead of use; automated portfolio-scale patience is the newer element.
attacks.ethical_notes: The entry is written around longitudinal and trajectory features defenders should monitor, and contains no conditioning schedule, timing guidance, or seasoning technique.

attacks.name: Analyst Feedback-Loop Poisoning And Retraining-Window Drift Exploitation
attacks.attacker_objective: Corrupt the labels and thresholds the fraud model retrains on, so that the defence itself is tuned to approve the attacker's traffic.
attacks.genai_mechanism: The attack surface is the defender's process rather than any single transaction: chargeback outcomes, analyst dispositions, and cardholder confirm-or-deny responses are the label supply. Generative tooling makes two things cheap at scale — coaching victims through personalised contact into confirming transactions as genuine, and producing large volumes of near-boundary traffic that pressures false-positive metrics until thresholds are relaxed. Campaigns can also be concentrated around seasonal periods when approval targets are loosened for volume, such as major festival sale windows.
attacks.transaction_signature: During the poisoning phase, deliberately unremarkable near-boundary traffic designed to be reviewed and cleared rather than to profit; after the drift lands, ordinary-looking fraud volume in the specific feature slice whose treatment was loosened. Neither phase has a distinctive authorisation footprint on its own.
attacks.behavioral_signature: Cohorts of transactions marked confirmed-legitimate that later attract disputes; confirmations arriving disproportionately through a single channel, or shortly after inbound contact with the cardholder; disputes withdrawn before resolution so the case closes as genuine; a narrow set of merchants, devices, or counterparties contributing an outsized share of recent training labels.
observable_signals: confirmed-legitimate cohorts converting to disputes at an abnormal rate
cardholder confirmations concentrated in one channel or following inbound contact
unusual rate of dispute withdrawals before resolution
small entity set contributing an outsized share of high-influence recent training data
approval rate jumping on a narrow feature slice immediately after retraining
false-positive pressure concentrated in one segment ahead of a threshold review
post_transaction_signals: delayed chargeback wave on transactions previously confirmed as genuine
loss rate rising in exactly the slice where thresholds were most recently relaxed
label-provenance audit finding clustering behind supposedly independent confirmations
recall requests on account-to-account transfers the customer earlier affirmed
attacks.real_world_grounding: Label noise and feedback-loop degradation are recognised failure modes in deployed fraud models, and coached-victim confirmation is a documented feature of social-engineering scams in Indian real-time payments; deliberate, sustained poisoning of the label pipeline as a campaign objective is a credible extrapolation rather than a widely documented case.
attacks.ethical_notes: It is written as model-governance guidance — label provenance auditing, post-retraining slice monitoring, and dispute-outcome reconciliation — and describes no method for generating decoy traffic or influencing analyst decisions.
